what: 1. Leaf traits and canopy structure: one row of parameters
title: 01. Getting Started with ToolsRTM
text: simulation always starts one row trait values – data.frame one column per parameter leaf canopy model need. , PROSPECT-D needs leaf biochemistry (N, Cab, Car, Anth, Cbrown, EWT, LMA); fourSAIL needs canopy structure (LAI, LIDFa/LIDFb/TypeLidf, hspot) sun-view geometry (tts/tto/psi): soil spectrum also required – foursail() mixes leaf optics whatever shows canopy gaps. 50/50 blend package’s bundled dry/wet reference soil spectra reasonable, physically-motivated default (Tutorial 05 covers building LUTs properly; Tutorial 10’s sibling article soil/MARMIT integration covers moisture-realistic alternative):
code: row <- data.frame(   # Canopy structure and geometry (fourSAIL)   LAI = 3, hspot = 0.01, LIDFa = -0.35, LIDFb = -0.15, TypeLidf = 1,   tts = 30, tto = 0, psi = 0,   # Leaf biochemistry (PROSPECT-D)   N = 1.5, Cab = 40, Car = 8, Anth = 2, Cbrown = 0, EWT = 0.009, LMA = 0.009,   alpha = 40 ) rsoil <- 0.5 * dataSpec_PDB[, 11] + 0.5 * dataSpec_PDB[, 12]  # dry/wet soil blend

title: 01. Getting Started with ToolsRTM
text: foursail() runs PROSPECT internally (via LeafModel argument) returns canopy-level outputs directly – ’s need call leaf model minimal example. LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D" selects leaf model; Tutorial 02 shows every leaf model available call PROSPECT leaf-level output needed.

title: 01. Getting Started with ToolsRTM
text: sail$rdot (hemispherical-directional reflectance factor) sail$rsot (bi-directional reflectance factor) fourSAIL’s two raw outputs. Compute_BRF() blends using sun/view geometry single top--canopy (TOC) reflectance spectrum sensor actually observes:
code: sail <- foursail(inputLUT = row, rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D") names(sail) #> [1] "rdot" "rsot" "rddt" "rsdt" reflectance <- Compute_BRF(rdot = sail$rdot, rsot = sail$rsot,                             tts = row$tts, data.light = dataSpec_PDB) length(reflectance)  # one value per nm, 400-2500nm #> [1] 2101

title: 01. Getting Started with ToolsRTM
text: familiar vegetation signature already visible: low reflectance visible (400-700nm, chlorophyll absorption), sharp rise red edge (~700-750nm), high NIR plateau (leaf/canopy structural scattering), two water-absorption dips SWIR (~1450nm, ~1950nm).
code: plot(dataSpec_PDB[, 1], reflectance, type = "l", col = "#2E8B57", lwd = 2,      xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "Reflectance",      main = "One simulation: fourSAIL + PROSPECT-D")

what: 1. Leaf radiative transfer: five models, called standalone
title: 02. From Leaf to Canopy Reflectance
text: ToolsRTM implements five leaf models. Three exported standalone functions (leaf-level , canopy); PROSPECT-D available bundled inside canopy call (foursail(..., LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D"), Section 2 ) – real asymmetry package’s exported API worth knowing rather guessing past.  Liberty (built needle leaves) reads visibly different two broadleaf-oriented models even comparable Cab/EWT – real structural difference, bug, since needle vs. broadleaf internal structure model represents.
code: pro <- prospect_PRO(N = 1.5, Cab = 40, Car = 8, Anth = 2, Cbrown = 0,                      EWT = 0.009, LMA = 0.009, alpha = 40, Prot = 0.002, CBC = 0.007)  lib_row <- data.frame(Cab = 40, EWT = 0.009, lign.cell = 2, Nitrogen = 1,                        cell.d = 40, inter.c = 0.045, baseline.abs = 0.0006,                        leaf.thick = 1.6, albino.abs = 0) lib <- liberty(lib_row)  flu_row <- data.frame(N = 1.8, Cab = 40, Car = 10, Anth = 0, EWT = 0.015,                        LMA = 0.01, Cs = 0.1, fqe = 0.01, Cx = 0, alpha = 40) flu <- getFluspect.B(inputsLeaf = flu_row, inputsOptipar = ToolsRTM::optipar, version = "D")  plot(pro$lambda, pro$refl, type = "l", col = "#0072B2", lwd = 2, ylim = c(0, 0.6),      xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "Leaf reflectance",      main = "Leaf reflectance: three models, similar Cab/EWT") lines(lib$lambda, lib$refl, col = "#009E73", lwd = 2) lines(flu$lambda, flu$refl, col = "#D55E00", lwd = 2) legend("topright", c("PROSPECT-PRO", "Liberty", "Fluspect-B"),        col = c("#0072B2", "#009E73", "#D55E00"), lwd = 2)

title: 02. From Leaf to Canopy Reflectance
text: fourSAIL, fourSAIL2, INFORM take kind leaf reflectance/transmittance turn canopy-level BRF, differ canopy structure represent – , correspondingly, extra parameters LUT needs: inform()’s return shape (bare vector, list(rdot=, rsot=)) real, useful--know inconsistency across three canopy functions – simulate_RTM() (used later tutorials) normalizes away, raw functions used directly .  INFORM’s forest-level reflectance sits visibly lower fourSAIL’s – expected, since INFORM’s explicit crown/shadow geometry isn’t present fourSAIL’s turbid-medium assumption. Tutorial 04 makes comparison systematic (5 leaf models x 3 canopy models, plus agreement/RMSE table); page mechanism, survey.
code: common_lut <- data.frame(   N = 1.5, Cab = 40, Car = 8, Anth = 1, Cbrown = 0, EWT = 0.01, LMA = 0.009, alpha = 40,   Prot = 0.002, CBC = 0.007, Cs = 0, fqe = 0.01, Cx = 0,   cell.d = 40, inter.c = 0.045, baseline.abs = 0.0006, leaf.thick = 1.6,   albino.abs = 0, lign.cell = 2, Nitrogen = 1,   LIDFa = -0.35, LIDFb = -0.15, TypeLidf = 1, LAI = 3, hspot = 0.01,   tts = 30, tto = 0, psi = 0,   fraction_brown = 0.1, diss = 0.5, Cv = 1, Zeta = 0,   LAIu = 0.5, sd = 650, cd = 4.5, h = 20, skyl = 0.1 ) rsoil <- rep(0.15, 2101) wl <- 400:2500  sim_foursail  <- foursail(inputLUT = common_lut, rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")$rsot sim_foursail2 <- foursail2(inputLUT = common_lut, rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")$rsot sim_inform    <- inform(inputLUT = common_lut, rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")  # bare vector  plot(wl, sim_foursail, type = "l", col = "#0072B2", lwd = 2, ylim = c(0, 0.5),      xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "TOC reflectance (rsot)",      main = "Canopy models: same LUT, same leaf model (PROSPECT-D)") lines(wl, sim_foursail2, col = "#009E73", lwd = 2) lines(wl, sim_inform, col = "#D55E00", lwd = 2) legend("topright", c("fourSAIL", "fourSAIL2", "INFORM"),        col = c("#0072B2", "#009E73", "#D55E00"), lwd = 2)

what: 3. How trait changes propagate: leaf sweeps that reach the canopy
title: 02. From Leaf to Canopy Reflectance
text: Sweep Cab EWT one time (everything else fixed) watch canopy-level spectrum respond – leaf--canopy chain preserves trait’s spectral signature, just attenuated/reshaped canopy:  trait leaves signature different spectral region – Cab visible/red-edge (chlorophyll absorption), EWT SWIR (water absorption), LAI mainly NIR plateau height (leaf layers, multiple scattering) visible saturates quickly canopy closed enough hide soil. Tutorial 10 formalizes proper global sensitivity analysis (Sobol/Johnson indices) rather one-trait---time sweeps.
code: sweep_trait <- function(trait, values) {   sapply(values, function(v) {     row2 <- common_lut; row2[[trait]] <- v     foursail(inputLUT = row2, rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")$rsot   }) } cab_curves <- sweep_trait("Cab", seq(10, 70, length.out = 6)) ewt_curves <- sweep_trait("EWT", seq(0.005, 0.03, length.out = 6)) lai_curves <- sweep_trait("LAI", seq(0.5, 7, length.out = 6))  op <- par(mfrow = c(3, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)) matplot(wl, cab_curves, type = "l", lty = 1, col = colorRampPalette(c("gold", "darkgreen"))(6),         xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "rsot", main = "Sweeping Cab (10-70 ug/cm2): visible/red-edge") matplot(wl, ewt_curves, type = "l", lty = 1, col = colorRampPalette(c("gold", "darkblue"))(6),         xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "rsot", main = "Sweeping EWT (0.005-0.03 g/cm2): SWIR") matplot(wl, lai_curves, type = "l", lty = 1, col = colorRampPalette(c("gold", "firebrick"))(6),         xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "rsot", main = "Sweeping LAI (0.5-7): NIR plateau + visible saturation") par(op)

title: 03. SPART: Soil-Plant-Atmosphere Radiative Transfer
text: Inputs fall five physical domains. inputsSPART (getLUT()-ready table, pattern inputsPROSAIL) already groups : Full argument documentation lives ?SPART – page focuses pieces fit together, exhaustive parameter list.
code: LUT <- as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = ToolsRTM::inputsSPART, nLUT = 5, setseed = 1)) # inputsSPART only ships PROSPECT-PRO/-D columns -- add what other leaf # models need too (same requirement as foursail()/SPART() itself). LUT$Cs <- 0; LUT$fqe <- 0.01; LUT$Cx <- 0 LUT$cell.d <- 40; LUT$inter.c <- 0.045; LUT$baseline.abs <- 0.0006 LUT$leaf.thick <- 1.6; LUT$albino.abs <- 0; LUT$lign.cell <- 2; LUT$Nitrogen <- 1 # A realistic, sea-level, clear-sky atmosphere for the worked example below # (getLUT()'s own default sampling range for the atmosphere columns is wide # enough to occasionally draw physically implausible combinations -- see # the note at the end of Section 3.2). LUT$Pa <- 1000; LUT$aot550 <- 0.3246; LUT$uo3 <- 0.3480; LUT$uh2o <- 1.4116 LUT$alt_m <- 0; LUT$Pa0 <- 1000

title: 03. SPART: Soil-Plant-Atmosphere Radiative Transfer
text: Unlike foursail(), SPART returns output already convolved chosen sensor’s bands (sensor.) – separate “simulate native, convolve” step (Tutorial 07 covers convolution foursail()/inform() output, stays 1nm resolution).  dip near 942nm near-total collapse near 1372nm real atmospheric water-vapour absorption bands – present TOA curve absent TOC, exactly real atmospheric correction deal . note getLUT()’s atmosphere sampling: wide default ranges inputsSPART samples , random rows combine high aot550 (aerosol loading) high alt_m (altitude) – combination SMAC’s atmospheric correction doesn’t handle gracefully, producing negative (physically meaningless) TOA reflectance. Always sanity-check range(sim$output$rfl.toa) random draw; fixed, realistic sea-level clear-sky atmosphere set Section 3.1 avoids rest page.
code: sim <- suppressWarnings(SPART(inputLUT = LUT[1, ], CanopyModel = "fourSAIL",                                LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO",                                sensor.i = ToolsRTM::Sentinel2A.MSI,                                rsoil = NULL, get.plots = FALSE)) names(sim$output)  # wave, rad.toa, rfl.toa, rfl.toc, rfl.toc.BRDF -- already at Sentinel-2A's own bands #> [1] "wave"         "rad.toa"      "rfl.toa"      "rfl.toc"      "rfl.toc.BRDF" plot(sim$output$wave, sim$output$rfl.toc.BRDF, type = "o", pch = 19, col = "#0072B2",      ylim = c(0, max(sim$output$rfl.toc.BRDF, sim$output$rfl.toa)),      xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "Reflectance", main = "SPART: TOC vs. TOA (Sentinel-2A bands)") lines(sim$output$wave, sim$output$rfl.toa, type = "o", pch = 19, col = "#D55E00") legend("topright", c("TOC (canopy)", "TOA (satellite)"), col = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00"), pch = 19, lty = 1)

title: 03. SPART: Soil-Plant-Atmosphere Radiative Transfer
text: Physically, sparse canopy let soil show dense one. Important caveat, found building page: psoil column documented inputsSPART/?SPART effect pass rsoil – SPART()’s built-BSM soil path (triggered whenever rsoil = NULL) hardcodes soil-moisture constants internally never reads inputLUT$psoil , sweeping psoil alone rsoil = NULL produces byte-identical output regardless value. demonstration uses explicit rsoil (foursail() already requires Tutorials 01-02) sidestep show real physics: Confirmed: soil brightness shifts sparse-canopy signal roughly 70x dense-canopy signal – canopy closes, soil brightness barely reaches sensor. page used two fixed flat rsoil spectra isolate LAI effect; physically-realistic moisture-driven soil spectrum instead arbitrary brightness value, see ToolsRTM::get.marmit.rsoil() (MARMIT, Bablet et al.) – plugs foursail()’s/foursail2()’s/inform()’s rsoil argument way, SPART()’s .
code:
soil_dark   <- rep(0.08, 2001)  # dark/wet-looking soil soil_bright <- rep(0.30, 2001)  # bright/dry-looking soil  soil_effect <- function(lai) {   row_i <- LUT[1, ]; row_i$LAI <- lai   d <- suppressWarnings(SPART(inputLUT = row_i, CanopyModel = "fourSAIL", LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO",                                sensor.i = ToolsRTM::Sentinel2A.MSI, rsoil = soil_dark, get.plots = FALSE))   b <- suppressWarnings(SPART(inputLUT = row_i, CanopyModel = "fourSAIL", LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO",                                sensor.i = ToolsRTM::Sentinel2A.MSI, rsoil = soil_bright, get.plots = FALSE))   mean(b$output$rfl.toc.BRDF) - mean(d$output$rfl.toc.BRDF) } cat("Mean TOC reflectance shift, dark vs. bright soil:
") #> Mean TOC reflectance shift, dark vs. bright soil: cat("  Sparse canopy (LAI=0.5):", round(soil_effect(0.5), 4), "
") #>   Sparse canopy (LAI=0.5): 0.1318 cat("  Dense canopy  (LAI=6):  ", round(soil_effect(6), 4), "
") #>   Dense canopy  (LAI=6):   0.0013 Low LAI                          High LAI   |                                 | large soil contribution     small soil contribution   |                                 | stronger background effect  canopy-dominated signal

title: 03. SPART: Soil-Plant-Atmosphere Radiative Transfer
text: Section 3.2’s plot already showed directly: compare rfl.toc.BRDF (canopy-level, atmosphere) rfl.toa (SMAC atmosphere layer) simulation. progression surface signal -> atmosphere -> sensor-observed signal, two curves diverge exactly atmospheric gases absorb strongly (water vapour, ozone), uniformly across spectrum.

title: 03. SPART: Soil-Plant-Atmosphere Radiative Transfer
text: tts (sun zenith), tto (view zenith), psi (relative azimuth) feed fourSAIL’s BRDF term inside SPART, way Compute_BRF() (Tutorial 01) – makes reflectance direction-dependent rather single fixed number per surface: Reflectance rises sun zenith angle (lower sun, longer optical path canopy, multiple scattering reaching sensor absorption) – direction-dependence BRDF means; Lambertian (direction-independent) assumption miss entirely.
code: for (tts_i in c(10, 30, 50)) {   row_i <- LUT[1, ]; row_i$tts <- tts_i   s_i <- suppressWarnings(SPART(inputLUT = row_i, CanopyModel = "fourSAIL", LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO",                                  sensor.i = ToolsRTM::Sentinel2A.MSI, rsoil = NULL, get.plots = FALSE))   cat("Sun zenith (tts) =", tts_i, "deg -> mean TOC BRDF:", round(mean(s_i$output$rfl.toc.BRDF), 4), "\n") } #> Sun zenith (tts) = 10 deg -> mean TOC BRDF: 0.1814 #> Sun zenith (tts) = 30 deg -> mean TOC BRDF: 0.1864 #> Sun zenith (tts) = 50 deg -> mean TOC BRDF: 0.1917

title: 03. SPART: Soil-Plant-Atmosphere Radiative Transfer
text: SPART already outputs chosen sensor’s bands, moving simulation realistic EO-like observation needs separate convolution step – just pick sensor.. sensors SPART actually supports (bundled objects ToolsRTM) listed :
code: spart_sensors <- c("LANDSAT4.TM", "LANDSAT5.TM", "LANDSAT7.ETM", "LANDSAT8.OLI",                     "Sentinel2A.MSI", "Sentinel2B.MSI", "Sentinel3A.OLCI",                     "Sentinel3B.OLCI", "TerraAqua.MODIS") s_modis <- suppressWarnings(SPART(inputLUT = LUT[1, ], CanopyModel = "fourSAIL", LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO",                                    sensor.i = ToolsRTM::TerraAqua.MODIS, rsoil = NULL, get.plots = FALSE)) cat("Sentinel-2A bands:", length(sim$output$wave), " -- MODIS bands:", length(s_modis$output$wave), "\n") #> Sentinel-2A bands: 13  -- MODIS bands: 20 Vegetation traits       + Canopy structure       + Soil       + Atmosphere       |       v     SPART       |       v Spectral observation, already at sensor bands       |       v Sentinel-2 / Landsat / MODIS / ...

Reach SPART() specifically question involves satellite actually measures TOA (atmospheric correction studies, comparing simulations directly uncorrected satellite products, workflow atmosphere’s contribution matters) – extra atmosphere/soil-BSM machinery needed otherwise.

title: 04. Comparing Radiative Transfer Models
code: df_leaf <- bind_rows(lapply(leaf_models, function(lm) {   short_domain <- lm %in% c("Fluspect-B", "Fluspect-B-Cx")   sim <- foursail(inputLUT = common_lut, rsoil = if (short_domain) rsoil_2001 else rsoil_2101,                    LeafModel = lm, spectrum.all = !short_domain)   data.frame(wavelength = if (short_domain) wl_2001 else wl_2101, rsot = sim$rsot, leaf_model = lm) })) ggplot(df_leaf, aes(x = wavelength, y = rsot, color = leaf_model)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) + scale_color_manual(values = leaf_colors) +   labs(title = "Leaf model comparison (canopy = fourSAIL)", x = "Wavelength (nm)",        y = "TOC reflectance (rsot)", color = "Leaf model") + theme_rtm

title: 04. Comparing Radiative Transfer Models
code: sim_foursail  <- foursail(inputLUT = common_lut, rsoil = rsoil_2101, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")$rsot sim_foursail2 <- foursail2(inputLUT = common_lut, rsoil = rsoil_2101, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")$rsot sim_inform    <- inform(inputLUT = common_lut, rsoil = rsoil_2101, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D") df_canopy <- bind_rows(   data.frame(wavelength = wl_2101, rsot = sim_foursail, model = "fourSAIL"),   data.frame(wavelength = wl_2101, rsot = sim_foursail2, model = "foursail2"),   data.frame(wavelength = wl_2101, rsot = sim_inform, model = "INFORM") ) ggplot(df_canopy, aes(x = wavelength, y = rsot, color = model)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +   labs(title = "Canopy model comparison (leaf = PROSPECT-D)", x = "Wavelength (nm)",        y = "TOC reflectance (rsot)", color = "Canopy model") + theme_rtm

title: 04. Comparing Radiative Transfer Models
text: Every leaf model x every canopy model supports , plus deviation--ensemble-mean heatmap – white means models agree wavelength, saturated colour means diverge:
code: df_grid <- bind_rows(lapply(canopy_models, function(cm) {   bind_rows(lapply(leaf_models, function(lm) {     short_domain <- lm %in% c("Fluspect-B", "Fluspect-B-Cx")     rsoil <- if (short_domain && cm != "INFORM") rsoil_2001 else rsoil_2101     sim <- tryCatch({       if (cm == "fourSAIL") foursail(inputLUT = common_lut, rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = lm, spectrum.all = !short_domain)$rsot       else if (cm == "foursail2") foursail2(inputLUT = common_lut, rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = lm)$rsot       else inform(inputLUT = common_lut, rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = lm)     }, error = function(e) NULL)     if (is.null(sim)) return(NULL)     data.frame(wavelength = if (short_domain) wl_2001 else wl_2101, rsot = sim, leaf_model = lm, canopy_model = cm)   })) })) df_grid$combo <- paste(df_grid$canopy_model, df_grid$leaf_model, sep = " + ")  ggplot(df_grid, aes(x = wavelength, y = rsot, color = leaf_model)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) + facet_wrap(~canopy_model) + scale_color_manual(values = leaf_colors) +   labs(title = "All canopy models x all leaf models", x = "Wavelength (nm)",        y = "TOC reflectance (rsot)", color = "Leaf model") + theme_rtm df_common <- df_grid[df_grid$wavelength <= 2400, ] %>%   group_by(wavelength) %>% mutate(ensemble_mean = mean(rsot), deviation = rsot - ensemble_mean) %>% ungroup()  ggplot(df_common, aes(x = wavelength, y = combo, fill = deviation)) +   geom_raster() +   scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", midpoint = 0, name = "rsot - mean") +   labs(title = "Where models agree and where they don't", x = "Wavelength (nm)", y = NULL) +   theme_rtm + theme(legend.position = "right", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))

what: Numeric agreement: RMSE vs. the ensemble mean
title: 04. Comparing Radiative Transfer Models
text: INFORM combinations sit furthest ensemble mean – expected, since explicit forest crown/shadow geometry represents genuinely different canopy structure fourSAIL/foursail2’s turbid-medium assumption, numerical disagreement resolved.
code: rmse_vs_mean <- df_common %>% group_by(combo) %>%   summarise(RMSE_vs_ensemble_mean = sqrt(mean(deviation^2)), .groups = "drop") %>%   arrange(desc(RMSE_vs_ensemble_mean)) knitr::kable(rmse_vs_mean, digits = 4)

what: 2. get_distributionLUT(): a different distribution per trait
title: 05. Building Look-Up Tables
text: Real leaf/canopy traits don’t follow distribution shape. Chlorophyll content (Cab) tends cluster around typical value (Gaussian-like); leaf-angle parameter LIDFa tendency across mixed canopy (closer Uniform). get_distributionLUT() lets trait pick shape instead forcing one distribution .  Cab (Gaussian) LIDFa (Uniform) came exact call – histograms show picking right distribution per trait matters.
code: minval <- data.frame('N' = 1.5, 'Cab' = 5, 'Car' = 0, 'Anth' = 0, 'Cbrown' = 0.0,                       'EWT' = 0.001, 'Prot' = 0.00001, 'CBC' = 0.00001,                       'LIDFa' = 0, 'LAI' = 0.5,                       LAIu = 0, sd = 200, cd = 0.2, h = 5,                       fraction_brown = 0, diss = 0.1, Cv = 0.3, Zeta = 0) maxval <- data.frame('N' = 3, 'Cab' = 70, 'Car' = 25, 'Anth' = 7, 'Cbrown' = 0.2,                       'EWT' = 0.035, 'Prot' = 0.03, 'CBC' = 0.03,                       'LIDFa' = 70, 'LAI' = 7,                       LAIu = 0.8, sd = 1000, cd = 7, h = 20,                       fraction_brown = 1, diss = 1, Cv = 1, Zeta = 0.2) TypeDistrib <- data.frame('N' = 'Gaussian', 'Cab' = 'Gaussian', 'Car' = 'Gaussian',                            'Anth' = 'Uniform', 'Cbrown' = 'Uniform',                            'EWT' = 'Uniform', 'Prot' = 'Uniform', 'CBC' = 'Uniform',                            'LIDFa' = 'Uniform', 'LAI' = 'Gaussian',                            LAIu = 'Uniform', sd = 'Uniform', cd = 'Uniform', h = 'Uniform',                            fraction_brown = 'Uniform', diss = 'Uniform', Cv = 'Uniform', Zeta = 'Uniform') Mean_gauss <- data.frame('N' = 2.2, 'Cab' = 45, 'Car' = 8, 'LAI' = 2.25) std_gauss <- Mean_gauss / 2.0  data.LUT <- get_distributionLUT(minval = minval, maxval = maxval, nSamples = 500,                                  TypeDistrib = TypeDistrib, Mean_gauss = Mean_gauss,                                  Std_gauss = std_gauss, DepCab = FALSE, setseed = 246) op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) hist(data.LUT$Cab, breaks = 30, col = "#2E8B57", border = "white",      main = "Cab (Gaussian, mean=45)", xlab = "Cab") hist(data.LUT$LIDFa, breaks = 30, col = "#B2182B", border = "white",      main = "LIDFa (Uniform)", xlab = "LIDFa") par(op)

title: 05. Building Look-Up Tables

title: 05. Building Look-Up Tables

title: 06. Large-Scale and Parallel RTM Simulation
code: t_seq <- system.time({   sims_seq <- lapply(seq_len(n.samples), function(i) {     sail_i <- foursail(inputLUT = LUT[i, ], rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")     sail_i$rsot   }) }) cat("Sequential:", round(t_seq[["elapsed"]], 2), "s for", n.samples, "simulations\n") #> Sequential: 3.3 s for 300 simulations

title: 06. Large-Scale and Parallel RTM Simulation
text: Three things matter pattern actually work, just look parallel: makeCluster()/registerDoParallel()/stopCluster() always paired – unclosed cluster leaks worker processes across whole R session, compounding chunk runs (e.g. re-knitting interactively). .packages = "ToolsRTM" inside foreach() – worker process starts fresh, packages attached; without , foursail() isn’t found workers every iteration errors. no_cores <- detectCores() - 2, detectCores() – leaves headroom OS R session’s main process, convention package’s course scripts (ForPROSAIL, Sensibility) use throughout.
code: no_cores <- max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 2) cl <- makeCluster(no_cores) registerDoParallel(cl)  t_par <- system.time({   sims_par <- foreach(i = 1:n.samples, .packages = "ToolsRTM") %dopar% {     sail_i <- foursail(inputLUT = LUT[i, ], rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")     sail_i$rsot   } }) stopCluster(cl)  cat("Parallel (", no_cores, "cores):", round(t_par[["elapsed"]], 2), "s for", n.samples, "simulations\n") #> Parallel ( 10 cores): 4.18 s for 300 simulations cat("Speedup:", round(t_seq[["elapsed"]] / t_par[["elapsed"]], 2), "x\n") #> Speedup: 0.79 x identical(sims_seq[[1]], sims_par[[1]])  # same result, sequential or parallel #> [1] TRUE

what: 4. When parallel is (and isn’t) worth it

Same green used for the # hyperspectral/dense-sensor overlay throughout this page (Sections 2-4). points(headwall_vnir_bands$wl, headwall_vnir_bands$RFL, col = "#2E8B57", pch = 19, cex = 0.8) legend("topright", c("Native 1nm", "Headwall VNIR"), col = c("grey70", "#2E8B57"), lty = c(1, NA), pch = c(NA, 19))

what: 6. Spectral sampling density, side by side
title: 08. Hyperspectral and VNIR Sensor Convolution
text: Approx_spacing_nm NA two irregular/mixed-sampling rows – 15-band rig places bands specific absorption features rather uniform steps, illustrative VNIR+SWIR row mixes real 2.23nm VNIR step representative 5nm SWIR step, single averaged number misrepresent .  “hyperspectral” buys multispectral, concretely: Sentinel-2A’s 13 bands can sample absorption features red-edge shape handful fixed points; PRISMA/EnMAP/Headwall’s 200+ narrow bands resolve actual continuous shape features – difference lets hyperspectral data support things multispectral can’t (e.g. narrowband indices centered exactly absorption feature, fitting absorption-feature depth/position directly rather inferring handful wide bands).

what: 1. Global sensitivity across the full spectrum: Johnson relative importance
title: 10. Understanding RTM Sensitivity
text: get.spectral.sensitivity() runs sensitivity::johnson() (Johnson relative-importance index) per wavelength – every trait varies simultaneously per simulation, unlike Tutorial 02’s OAT sweeps. real bug found fixed building page: function’s name earlier draft page said “Sobol total index” – get.sobol.indices() (get.spectral.sensitivity() calls internally) compute Sobol total index (STi), specific column genuine formula bug (accidentally squares output instead using input trait , every trait came nearly value – telltale symptom Cab, EWT, LAI landing within percentage point every wavelength, including right next 400 vs 410nm, physical reason flat). Fixed switching get.sobol.indices()’s separately, correctly computed .Johnson_norm column (sensitivity::johnson(), different code path function) – metric package’s reference sensitivity scripts already use exact kind figure. STi_pct column name kept backward compatibility even though Johnson-based now, Sobol-based.  number lands exactly leaf/canopy optics theory says – Cab visible, EWT water bands, LAI NIR – concrete confirmation fix produced real physics, another plausible-looking wrong pattern. Cab dominates visible, EWT SWIR water-absorption region – consistent Tutorial 02’s OAT sweeps, now every trait varying jointly rather one time.
code:
si <- get.spectral.sensitivity(n.samples = 200, distribution = "Uniform",                                 traits = c("Cab", "EWT", "LAI"), wl.step = 10,                                 seed = 1, chunk.size = 200, save.path = tempfile()) head(si) #>   wavelength    trait    STi_pct distribution #> 1        400      Cab 49.4423550      Uniform #> 2        400      EWT  0.6056136      Uniform #> 3        400      LAI 48.1633645      Uniform #> 4        400 SoilCoef  1.7886668      Uniform #> 5        410      Cab 44.3162064      Uniform #> 6        410      EWT  0.5210568      Uniform ggplot(si, aes(x = wavelength, y = STi_pct, fill = trait)) +   geom_area(position = "stack") +   labs(title = "Spectral sensitivity of TOC reflectance (fourSAIL + PROSPECT-D)",        subtitle = sprintf("Johnson relative-importance index, %d simulations", 200),        x = "Wavelength (nm)", y = "Relative importance [%]") +   theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "bottom") cab <- subset(si, trait == "Cab"); ewt <- subset(si, trait == "EWT"); lai <- subset(si, trait == "LAI") cat("Cab: ", round(mean(cab$STi_pct[cab$wavelength >= 430 & cab$wavelength <= 680]), 1),     "% in the visible/red absorption region (430-680nm), only ",     round(mean(cab$STi_pct[cab$wavelength >= 750 & cab$wavelength <= 1300]), 1),     "% in the NIR plateau (750-1300nm, no chlorophyll absorption feature there)
", sep = "") #> Cab: 84.5% in the visible/red absorption region (430-680nm), only 0.9% in the NIR plateau (750-1300nm, no chlorophyll absorption feature there) cat("EWT: ", round(mean(ewt$STi_pct[ewt$wavelength >= 1400 & ewt$wavelength <= 1500]), 1),     "% near the 1450nm water-absorption band, only ",     round(mean(ewt$STi_pct[ewt$wavelength >= 430 & ewt$wavelength <= 680]), 1),     "% in the visible (no water absorption feature there)
", sep = "") #> EWT: 98.8% near the 1450nm water-absorption band, only 0.8% in the visible (no water absorption feature there) cat("LAI: ", round(mean(lai$STi_pct[lai$wavelength >= 750 & lai$wavelength <= 1300]), 1),     "% in the NIR plateau (structural multiple scattering) -- the leaf-count/canopy-structure signal
", sep = "") #> LAI: 72.8% in the NIR plateau (structural multiple scattering) -- the leaf-count/canopy-structure signal

what: 2. Global Sobol sensitivity, per Sentinel-2A band
title: 10. Understanding RTM Sensitivity
text: proper quasi-random Sobol design (sensobol::sobol_matrices()), giving first-order (Si) total (Ti) indices per band rather per native wavelength:  LAI dominates NIR band (B8); pigments (Cab/Car) dominate red band (B4) – exactly leaf/canopy optics theory predicts.
code: library(sensobol) params <- c("Cab", "Car", "LAI", "EWT") N <- 40  # base sample size; total simulations = N * (length(params) + 2) mat01 <- sobol_matrices(N = N, params = params) ranges <- list(Cab = c(5, 90), Car = c(0.5, 25), LAI = c(0.5, 7), EWT = c(0.001, 0.035))  LUT_sobol <- as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL, nLUT = nrow(mat01), setseed = 1234)) for (p in params) LUT_sobol[[p]] <- ranges[[p]][1] + mat01[, p] * diff(ranges[[p]])  rsoil <- rep(0.15, 2101) refl <- t(sapply(seq_len(nrow(LUT_sobol)), function(i) {   foursail(inputLUT = LUT_sobol[i, ], rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")$rsot })) colnames(refl) <- paste0("R.", 400:2500) refl_X <- as.data.frame(refl); colnames(refl_X) <- paste0("X", 400:2500); refl_X <- cbind(id = seq_len(nrow(refl_X)), refl_X) se2a <- suppressMessages(get.spectra.convolved(rfl = refl_X, sensor = "Sentinel2a", plot.spectra = FALSE)) #> [1] "Spectral resampling function to SENTINEL2A is being processed ..." #>   |                                                                              |                                                                      |   0%  | lapply(c("B4", "B8", "B11"), function(band) {   ind <- sobol_indices(Y = se2a[[band]], N = N, params = params)   data.frame(Band = band, Parameter = ind$results$parameters, Index = ind$results$original, Type = ind$results$sensitivity) })) ggplot(subset(sobol_df, Type == "Ti"), aes(x = Band, y = Index, fill = Parameter)) +   geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") + plot.spectra = FALSE)) #> [1] "Spectral resampling function to SENTINEL2A is being processed ..." #>   |                                                                              | c("Cab", "Car", "Anth", "LMA", "Cbrown", "N", "LIDFa", "LAI", "EWT") X <- LUT_j[, candidate_traits] # PROSPECT-PRO leaves LMA constant (uses Prot/CBC for dry matter instead) -- # johnson()'s correlation-matrix step fails outright on a zero-variance # column, so drop any before calling it. zero_var <- sapply(X, function(v) sd(v) == 0) if (any(zero_var)) { cat("Dropping zero-variance what: A practical note on zero-variance predictors
title: 10. Understanding RTM Sensitivity
text: Building Johnson section surfaced real, generically-useful gotcha: johnson()’s correlation-matrix step fails outright (eigen(): infinite missing values) predictor column zero variance – e.g. LMA constant LUT built LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO", since variant uses CBC/Prot dry matter instead. Always check drop constant columns feeding LUT-derived data.frame correlation- regression-based sensitivity method.

title: 11. From Physics to Vegetation Traits: Hybrid Inversion
text: method picks “closeness” two spectra measured. nOpt controls many closest training spectra get averaged together final trait estimate: call returns 2-element list: [[1]] (rfl.b) matched reflectance , [[2]] (LUT.best) corresponding trait table: merit-RMSE/merit-FGE compare raw band reflectance; merit-DWT compares spectrum’s discrete wavelet transform coefficients instead (sensitive overall spectral shape rather band’s exact value). merit-NRMSE, merit-MAE, merit-NMB, merit-1stD (first-derivative matching) remaining built-options; custom_stat accepts function(sim, obs).
code: opt_rmse <- get.inversionOpt(rfl.sensor = se2a_test_mat, rfl.rtm = se2a_train_mat,                               LUT = LUT_train, wave = wl_bands, method = "merit-RMSE", nOpt = 5) opt_fge  <- get.inversionOpt(rfl.sensor = se2a_test_mat, rfl.rtm = se2a_train_mat,                               LUT = LUT_train, wave = wl_bands, method = "merit-FGE", nOpt = 5) opt_dwt  <- get.inversionOpt(rfl.sensor = se2a_test_mat, rfl.rtm = se2a_train_mat,                               LUT = LUT_train, wave = wl_bands, method = "merit-DWT", nOpt = 5) opt_metrics <- data.frame(   method = c("merit-RMSE", "merit-FGE", "merit-DWT"),   R2   = c(r2_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_rmse[[2]]$Cab), r2_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_fge[[2]]$Cab), r2_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_dwt[[2]]$Cab)),   RMSE = c(rmse_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_rmse[[2]]$Cab), rmse_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_fge[[2]]$Cab), rmse_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_dwt[[2]]$Cab)) ) knitr::kable(opt_metrics, digits = 3) plot(LUT_test$Cab, opt_rmse[[2]]$Cab, pch = 19, col = "#2166AC",      xlab = "Observed Cab", ylab = "Predicted Cab (merit-RMSE, nOpt=5)",      main = "LUT merit-function matching") abline(0, 1, col = "grey40", lty = 2)

title: 14. End-to-End RTM Inversion Pipeline
text: simulate_RTM() dispatches foursail()/foursail2()/inform() based canopy.model – canopy.model single variable, separate script per model:
code: run_pipeline <- function(canopy.model, leaf.model = "PROSPECT-D", n.samples = 500, seed = 1) {   LUT <- as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL, nLUT = n.samples, setseed = seed))   LUT$Cs <- 0; LUT$fqe <- 0.01; LUT$Cx <- 0   LUT$cell.d <- 40; LUT$inter.c <- 0.045; LUT$baseline.abs <- 0.0006   LUT$leaf.thick <- 1.6; LUT$albino.abs <- 0; LUT$lign.cell <- 2; LUT$Nitrogen <- 1   LUT$fraction_brown <- 0.1; LUT$diss <- 0.5; LUT$Cv <- 1; LUT$Zeta <- 0   LUT$LAIu <- 0.5; LUT$sd <- 650; LUT$cd <- 4.5; LUT$h <- 20; LUT$skyl <- 0.1    rsoil <- rep(0.15, 2101)   # 500 simulations per canopy model, x3 models -- parallelized the same way   # as Tutorial 06, rather than a plain sapply(), to keep this vignette's   # build time reasonable at this sample size.   no_cores <- max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 2)   cl <- makeCluster(no_cores)   registerDoParallel(cl)   refl_list <- foreach(i = seq_len(n.samples), .packages = "ToolsRTM") %dopar% {     suppressMessages(simulate_RTM(inputLUT = LUT[i, ], rsoil = rsoil,                                    leaf.model = leaf.model, canopy.model = canopy.model))$rsot   }   stopCluster(cl)   refl <- do.call(rbind, refl_list)   colnames(refl) <- paste0("R.", 400:2500)    refl_X <- as.data.frame(refl); colnames(refl_X) <- paste0("X", 400:2500); refl_X <- cbind(id = seq_len(n.samples), refl_X)   se2a <- suppressMessages(get.spectra.convolved(rfl = refl_X, sensor = "Sentinel2a", plot.spectra = FALSE))   band_names <- paste0("B", seq_along(as.numeric(names(se2a)[-1])))   names(se2a) <- c("id", band_names)    train_idx <- sample(seq_len(n.samples), size = round(0.7 * n.samples))   train_df <- cbind(LUT[train_idx, ], se2a[train_idx, band_names])   test_df  <- cbind(LUT[-train_idx, ], se2a[-train_idx, band_names])    fit <- get.inversion(data = train_df, depVar = "LAI", inputs = band_names,                         algorithm = "RF", n.samples = nrow(train_df), seed = 42)   pred <- as.numeric(predict(fit$model, newdata = test_df[, c("LAI", band_names)]))   r2 <- 1 - sum((test_df$LAI - pred)^2) / sum((test_df$LAI - mean(test_df$LAI))^2)    list(LUT = LUT, refl = refl, obs = test_df$LAI, pred = pred, r2 = r2) }

what: 1. Retrieve a real Sentinel-2 image via STAC
title: 15. From Satellite Reflectance to Vegetation Traits: Real EO Application
text: ToolsRTM::get.satellite_collection() searches signs STAC collection (Microsoft Planetary Computer default); get.sentinel2_cube() builds actual gridded raster cube chosen area/date range (gdalcubes hood). real, exported package functions – ones Apps/STAC’s Shiny app uses. Wrapped tryCatch() since live network/STAC access inherently less reliable documentation build local simulation: get.sentinel2_cube() already masks clouds/shadows/snow via SCL band mean-aggregates every cloud-free date range onto one 20m grid – one real, composited scene, single tile single overpass.
code: retrieval <- tryCatch({   library(sf)   # Wageningen, NL -- open farmland, a plausible study area for this package   pt <- st_point(c(5.6667, 51.9667)) |> st_sfc(crs = 4326)   scenario <- st_as_sf(data.frame(id = 1), geometry = st_sfc(pt[[1]], crs = 4326))    sc <- get.satellite_collection(scenario = scenario, collection = "sentinel-2-l2a",                                   cloud_server = "microsoft", n.limit = 20,                                   date_range = c("2024-06-01", "2024-08-31"),                                   cloud_threshold = 20, buffer_size = 1500)    bbox <- get_bounding_box(scenario, 1500)   shape <- st_as_sf(data.frame(id = 1), geometry = st_sfc(st_polygon(list(rbind(     c(bbox["xmin"], bbox["ymin"]), c(bbox["xmin"], bbox["ymax"]),     c(bbox["xmax"], bbox["ymax"]), c(bbox["xmax"], bbox["ymin"]),     c(bbox["xmin"], bbox["ymin"])))), crs = 4326))    cube <- get.sentinel2_cube(sc[[1]], shape = shape, date_range = c("2024-06-01", "2024-08-31"),                               aggregation_method = "mean", get.dataset = FALSE)   list(ok = TRUE, cube = cube) }, error = function(e) list(ok = FALSE, msg = conditionMessage(e)))  if (!retrieval$ok) {   cat("STAC retrieval skipped -- no network/STAC access from this build environment (",       retrieval$msg, "). Everything below needs `retrieval$cube` and is skipped too.\n") } if (retrieval$ok) {   cube <- retrieval$cube   cat("Real Sentinel-2 cube retrieved:", paste(dim(cube), collapse = " x "),       "(rows x cols x bands), bands:", paste(names(cube), collapse = ", "), "\n") } #> Real Sentinel-2 cube retrieved: 161 x 161 x 11 (rows x cols x bands), bands: B02, B03, B04, B05, B06, B07, B08, B8A, B11, B12, SCL

what: 3. Train a hybrid-inversion model on a SIMULATED LUT
title: 15. From Satellite Reflectance to Vegetation Traits: Real EO Application
text: pattern Tutorials 10-13 – model trained entirely foursail() simulations, never real data. training bands must match real cube actually provides: get.spectra.convolved() returns Sentinel-2A’s full 13-band set (B1-B12, including 60m bands); subset 10 cube , rename match:
code: if (retrieval$ok) {   n_samples <- 150   LUT <- as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL, nLUT = n_samples, setseed = 1))   wl <- 400:2500; rsoil <- rep(0.15, length(wl))   sim_refl <- t(sapply(seq_len(n_samples), function(i) {     foursail(inputLUT = LUT[i, ], rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO")$rsot   }))   refl_X <- as.data.frame(sim_refl); colnames(refl_X) <- paste0("X", wl)   refl_X <- cbind(id = seq_len(n_samples), refl_X)   se2a_full <- suppressMessages(get.spectra.convolved(rfl = refl_X, sensor = "Sentinel2a", plot.spectra = FALSE))   names(se2a_full) <- c("id","B1","B2","B3","B4","B5","B6","B7","B8","B8A","B9","B10","B11","B12")    keep <- c("B2","B3","B4","B5","B6","B7","B8","B8A","B11","B12")       # matches the cube's 10 bands   real_names <- c("B02","B03","B04","B05","B06","B07","B08","B8A","B11","B12")   se2a <- se2a_full[, keep]; names(se2a) <- real_names    train_df <- cbind(LUT, se2a)   fit <- get.inversion(data = train_df, depVar = "LAI", inputs = real_names,                         algorithm = "RF", n.samples = nrow(train_df), seed = 42) }

title: 15. From Satellite Reflectance to Vegetation Traits: Real EO Application
text: Every pixel’s 10-band reflectance goes fitted model – building block ToolsRTM::getSpatialTrait() uses internally (pixel extraction, prediction, reassembled back raster), done explicitly self-contained:  real, per-pixel trait map – retrieved simulated page, verified end end, illustrative mockup.
code: if (retrieval$ok) {   pix_df <- as.data.frame(refl_cube, xy = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE)   ok_rows <- complete.cases(pix_df[, real_names])   pred_lai <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(pix_df))   pred_lai[ok_rows] <- as.numeric(predict(fit$model, newdata = pix_df[ok_rows, real_names]))    lai_rast <- refl_cube[["B04"]]  # reuse its grid/extent/crs   values(lai_rast) <- pred_lai   names(lai_rast) <- "LAI_pred"    plot(lai_rast, main = "Real Sentinel-2 pixels -> hybrid-inverted LAI (trained on simulated LUT)")   cat("Predicted LAI range across the scene:", paste(round(range(pred_lai, na.rm = TRUE), 2), collapse = " to "), "\n") } #> Predicted LAI range across the scene: 2.95 to 3.73

SPART() (Tutorial 03) carries MARMIT soil spectrum full soil-plant-atmosphere chain TOA – question section answers Tutorial 03 doesn’t: soil-moisture signal still visible atmosphere, get washed ? code: soils_spart <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(wetness_steps)), function(i) {   get.marmit.rsoil(database = "Bablet_2016", id = 1, L = wetness_steps$L[i],                     eps = wetness_steps$eps[i], wl.out = 400:2400) })  LUT <- as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = ToolsRTM::inputsSPART, nLUT = 1, setseed = 1)) LUT$Cs <- 0; LUT$fqe <- 0.01; LUT$Cx <- 0 LUT$cell.d <- 40; LUT$inter.c <- 0.045; LUT$baseline.abs <- 0.0006 LUT$leaf.thick <- 1.6; LUT$albino.abs <- 0; LUT$lign.cell <- 2; LUT$Nitrogen <- 1 LUT$Pa <- 1000; LUT$aot550 <- 0.3246; LUT$uo3 <- 0.3480; LUT$uh2o <- 1.4116 LUT$alt_m <- 0; LUT$Pa0 <- 1000 LUT$LAI <- 1.5  # sparse enough that soil still reaches the sensor (Section 3's lesson)  spart_by_soil <- lapply(soils_spart, function(s) {   suppressWarnings(SPART(inputLUT = LUT[1, ], CanopyModel = "fourSAIL", LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO",                           sensor.i = ToolsRTM::Sentinel2A.MSI, rsoil = s$rsoil.wet, get.plots = FALSE)) })  toc_means <- sapply(spart_by_soil, function(s) mean(s$output$rfl.toc.BRDF)) toa_means <- sapply(spart_by_soil, function(s) mean(s$output$rfl.toa)) comparison <- data.frame(Wetness = wetness_steps$label, SMC_pct = round(sapply(soils_spart, function(s) s$SMC), 1),                           Mean_TOC = round(toc_means, 4), Mean_TOA = round(toa_means, 4)) knitr::kable(comparison) plot(wetness_steps$eps, toc_means, type = "o", pch = 19, col = "#2166AC",      ylim = range(c(toc_means, toa_means)),      xlab = "Wetness fraction (eps)", ylab = "Mean reflectance (Sentinel-2A bands)",      main = "Soil moisture -> TOC vs. TOA (SPART, LAI=1.5)") lines(wetness_steps$eps, toa_means, type = "o", pch = 19, col = "#D55E00") legend("topright", c("TOC (canopy)", "TOA (satellite)"), col = c("#2166AC", "#D55E00"), pch = 19, lty = 1)

what: 2. Train RF models for Cab, LAI, and EWT on a simulated LUT
title: 17. Monitoring a Forest Site Through Time
text: pattern Tutorials 10-11 14 – trained entirely foursail() simulations, 10 bands real cube provides:
code: n_samples <- 200 LUT <- as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL, nLUT = n_samples, setseed = 1)) wl <- 400:2500; rsoil <- rep(0.15, length(wl)) sim_refl <- t(sapply(seq_len(n_samples), function(i) {   foursail(inputLUT = LUT[i, ], rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO")$rsot })) refl_X <- as.data.frame(sim_refl); colnames(refl_X) <- paste0("X", wl) refl_X <- cbind(id = seq_len(n_samples), refl_X) se2a_full <- suppressMessages(get.spectra.convolved(rfl = refl_X, sensor = "Sentinel2a", plot.spectra = FALSE)) names(se2a_full) <- c("id","B1","B2","B3","B4","B5","B6","B7","B8","B8A","B9","B10","B11","B12") keep <- c("B2","B3","B4","B5","B6","B7","B8","B8A","B11","B12") real_names <- c("B02","B03","B04","B05","B06","B07","B08","B8A","B11","B12") se2a <- se2a_full[, keep]; names(se2a) <- real_names train_df <- cbind(LUT, se2a)  fits <- lapply(c("Cab", "LAI", "EWT"), function(trait) {   get.inversion(data = train_df, depVar = trait, inputs = real_names,                 algorithm = "RF", n.samples = nrow(train_df), seed = 42) }) names(fits) <- c("Cab", "LAI", "EWT")

what: 3. Retrieve a real time series and invert each date
title: 17. Monitoring a Forest Site Through Time
text: One STAC search + cube retrieval per monthly window, spatially averaged site (terra::global(..., "mean")) – real network round-trip per date, wrapped tryCatch() since individual date can fail ordinary reasons (cloud-free scene month, transient STAC issues):
code: windows <- list(c("2024-03-01","2024-03-31"), c("2024-05-01","2024-05-31"),                  c("2024-07-01","2024-07-31"), c("2024-09-01","2024-09-30"),                  c("2024-11-01","2024-11-30"))  get_one_date <- function(w) {   tryCatch({     sc <- get.satellite_collection(scenario = scenario, collection = "sentinel-2-l2a",                                     cloud_server = "microsoft", n.limit = 20,                                     date_range = w, cloud_threshold = 40, buffer_size = 300)     if (is.null(sc[[1]])) stop("no cloud-free items this window")     cube <- get.sentinel2_cube(sc[[1]], shape = shape, date_range = w,                                 aggregation_method = "mean", get.dataset = FALSE)     refl <- cube[[c("B02","B03","B04","B05","B06","B07","B08","B8A","B11","B12")]] / 10000     means <- as.numeric(terra::global(refl, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[, 1])     names(means) <- real_names     if (any(!is.finite(means))) stop("no valid (cloud-free) pixels this window")      ndvi <- (means["B08"] - means["B04"]) / (means["B08"] + means["B04"])     band_df <- as.data.frame(t(means))     preds <- sapply(fits, function(f) as.numeric(predict(f$model, newdata = band_df)))      data.frame(date = as.Date(w[1]), NDVI = as.numeric(ndvi),                Cab = preds["Cab"], LAI = preds["LAI"], EWT = preds["EWT"], ok = TRUE, msg = "")   }, error = function(e) data.frame(date = as.Date(w[1]), NDVI = NA_real_, Cab = NA_real_,                                      LAI = NA_real_, EWT = NA_real_,                                      ok = FALSE, msg = conditionMessage(e))) }  ts_list <- lapply(windows, get_one_date) ts_df <- do.call(rbind, ts_list) print(ts_df) #>            date      NDVI      Cab      LAI         EWT    ok #> 1    2024-03-01        NA       NA       NA          NA FALSE #> Cab  2024-05-01 0.5281266 13.22195 3.444244 0.007849854  TRUE #> Cab1 2024-07-01 0.5356662 13.91773 3.470848 0.007451011  TRUE #> Cab2 2024-09-01 0.5011458 14.52651 3.200938 0.005419384  TRUE #> Cab3 2024-11-01 0.3504465 14.98811 3.073729 0.004877992  TRUE #>                                           msg #> 1    no valid (cloud-free) pixels this window #> Cab                                           #> Cab1                                          #> Cab2                                          #> Cab3

what: 1. Simulate a 500-row LUT and invert Cab
title: 18. Data-Driven Spatial Index Mapping with getSpatial_index()
text: rigor Tutorial 12 – 500 simulations, Sentinel-2A convolution, Random Forest, held-test set:
code: n_samples <- 500 LUT <- as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL, nLUT = n_samples, setseed = 1)) wl <- 400:2500; rsoil <- rep(0.15, length(wl)) refl <- t(sapply(seq_len(n_samples), function(i) {   foursail(inputLUT = LUT[i, ], rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO")$rsot })) refl_X <- as.data.frame(refl); colnames(refl_X) <- paste0("X", wl); refl_X <- cbind(id = seq_len(n_samples), refl_X) se2a_full <- suppressMessages(get.spectra.convolved(rfl = refl_X, sensor = "Sentinel2a", plot.spectra = FALSE)) names(se2a_full) <- c("id","B1","B2","B3","B4","B5","B6","B7","B8","B8A","B9","B10","B11","B12")  keep <- c("B2","B3","B4","B5","B6","B7","B8","B8A","B11","B12") real_names <- c("B02","B03","B04","B05","B06","B07","B08","B8A","B11","B12") se2a <- se2a_full[, keep]; names(se2a) <- real_names  set.seed(1) train_idx <- sample(seq_len(n_samples), size = round(0.7 * n_samples)) train_df <- cbind(LUT[train_idx, ], se2a[train_idx, ]) fit_cab <- get.inversion(data = train_df, depVar = "Cab", inputs = real_names,                           algorithm = "RF", n.samples = nrow(train_df), seed = 42)

text: Two independent pixel--pixel outputs real scene – one plain spectral index, full hybrid-inversion trait retrieval – spatial agreement (disagreement) informative, assumed: strong correlation means simple index largely capturing signal expensive ML model ; weak one means ML model picking something index alone misses.
code: pix_df <- as.data.frame(refl, xy = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE) ok_rows <- stats::complete.cases(pix_df[, real_names]) Cab_pixels <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(pix_df)) Cab_pixels[ok_rows] <- as.numeric(predict(fit_cab$model, pix_df[ok_rows, real_names]))  cab_map <- refl[["B04"]] terra::values(cab_map) <- Cab_pixels names(cab_map) <- "Cab_pred"  op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) plot(idx_map[[1]], main = winning_index) plot(cab_map, main = "Retrieved Cab") par(op)  cat("Correlation between the mapped", winning_index, "and mapped Cab, pixel-by-pixel:",     round(cor(as.numeric(terra::values(idx_map[[1]])), Cab_pixels, use = "complete.obs"), 2), "\n") #> Correlation between the mapped REIP1 and mapped Cab, pixel-by-pixel: 0.21

what: 1. get_distributionLUT(): a different distribution per trait
title: Getting-LUTs
text: Real leaf/canopy traits don’t follow distribution shape. Chlorophyll content (Cab) tends cluster around typical value (Gaussian-like); leaf-angle parameter LIDFa tendency across mixed canopy (closer Uniform). get_distributionLUT() lets trait pick shape instead forcing one distribution . Define sampling range (minval/maxval, one column per trait) , separately, distribution trait uses: Traits marked "Gaussian" need mean standard deviation (traits left Mean_gauss/Std_gauss – everything "Uniform" – simply ignored part):
code: minval <- data.frame('N' = 1.5, 'Cab' = 5, 'Car' = 0, 'Anth' = 0, 'Cbrown' = 0.0,                       'EWT' = 0.001, 'Prot' = 0.00001, 'CBC' = 0.00001,                       'LIDFa' = 0, 'LAI' = 0.5,                       ### input for INFORM                       LAIu = 0, sd = 200, cd = 0.2, h = 5,                       ### input for fourSAIL-2                       fraction_brown = 0, diss = 0.1, Cv = 0.3, Zeta = 0)  maxval <- data.frame('N' = 3, 'Cab' = 70, 'Car' = 25, 'Anth' = 7, 'Cbrown' = 0.2,                       'EWT' = 0.035, 'Prot' = 0.03, 'CBC' = 0.03,                       'LIDFa' = 70, 'LAI' = 7,                       ### input for INFORM                       LAIu = 0.8, sd = 1000, cd = 7, h = 20,                       ### input for fourSAIL-2                       fraction_brown = 1, diss = 1, Cv = 1, Zeta = 0.2)  TypeDistrib <- data.frame('N' = 'Gaussian', 'Cab' = 'Gaussian', 'Car' = 'Gaussian',                            'Anth' = 'Uniform', 'Cbrown' = 'Uniform',                            'EWT' = 'Uniform', 'Prot' = 'Uniform', 'CBC' = 'Uniform',                            'LIDFa' = 'Uniform', 'LAI' = 'Gaussian',                            ### input for INFORM                            LAIu = 'Uniform', sd = 'Uniform', cd = 'Uniform', h = 'Uniform',                            ### input for fourSAIL-2                            fraction_brown = 'Uniform', diss = 'Uniform', Cv = 'Uniform', Zeta = 'Uniform') Mean_gauss <- data.frame('N' = 2.2, 'Cab' = 45, 'Car' = 8, 'LAI' = 2.25) std_gauss <- Mean_gauss / 2.0 nSamples <- 500 data.LUT <- get_distributionLUT(minval = minval, maxval = maxval,                                  nSamples = nSamples, TypeDistrib = TypeDistrib,                                  Mean_gauss = Mean_gauss, Std_gauss = std_gauss,                                  DepCab = FALSE, setseed = 246)

title: Trait inversion: merit-function matching, ML, and deep learning
text: 70/30 split feeds get.inversionOpt() (reference LUT vs. “observed” test spectra), get.inversion() (training data vs. prediction targets), getMLmodel() – comparison end apples--apples.
code: set.seed(1) train_idx <- sample(seq_len(n_samples), size = round(0.7 * n_samples)) test_idx  <- setdiff(seq_len(n_samples), train_idx)  LUT_train <- LUT[train_idx, ] LUT_test  <- LUT[test_idx, ] se2a_mat  <- as.matrix(se2a[, band_names]) se2a_train_mat <- se2a_mat[train_idx, ] se2a_test_mat  <- se2a_mat[test_idx, ]  train_df <- cbind(LUT_train, se2a[train_idx, band_names]) test_df  <- cbind(LUT_test,  se2a[test_idx,  band_names])  r2_f   <- function(obs, pred) 1 - sum((obs - pred)^2) / sum((obs - mean(obs))^2) rmse_f <- function(obs, pred) sqrt(mean((obs - pred)^2))  cat("Train:", length(train_idx), "spectra. Test (held out):", length(test_idx), "spectra.\n") #> Train: 105 spectra. Test (held out): 45 spectra.

title: Trait inversion: merit-function matching, ML, and deep learning
text: method picks “closeness” two spectra measured. nOpt controls many closest training spectra get averaged together final trait estimate (nOpt = 5 – compromise single nearest neighbour, noisy, averaging many, smooths real trait variation): call returns 2-element list: [[1]] (rfl.b) matched reflectance , [[2]] (LUT.best) corresponding trait table – including merit-function’s error value (merit-RMSE, merit-FGE, …) Cab estimate ’re evaluating : merit-RMSE/merit-FGE compare raw band reflectance; merit-DWT compares spectrum’s discrete wavelet transform coefficients instead (sensitive overall shape spectrum rather band’s exact value – can robust band--band noise). merit-NRMSE, merit-MAE, merit-NMB merit-1stD (first-derivative matching, sensitive absorption-feature position/shape absolute reflectance) remaining built-options; custom_stat accepts function(sim, obs) returning single error value place .
code: opt_rmse <- get.inversionOpt(rfl.sensor = se2a_test_mat, rfl.rtm = se2a_train_mat,                               LUT = LUT_train, wave = wl_bands, method = "merit-RMSE", nOpt = 5) opt_fge  <- get.inversionOpt(rfl.sensor = se2a_test_mat, rfl.rtm = se2a_train_mat,                               LUT = LUT_train, wave = wl_bands, method = "merit-FGE", nOpt = 5) opt_dwt  <- get.inversionOpt(rfl.sensor = se2a_test_mat, rfl.rtm = se2a_train_mat,                               LUT = LUT_train, wave = wl_bands, method = "merit-DWT", nOpt = 5) opt_metrics <- data.frame(   method = c("merit-RMSE", "merit-FGE", "merit-DWT"),   R2   = c(r2_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_rmse[[2]]$Cab), r2_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_fge[[2]]$Cab), r2_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_dwt[[2]]$Cab)),   RMSE = c(rmse_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_rmse[[2]]$Cab), rmse_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_fge[[2]]$Cab), rmse_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_dwt[[2]]$Cab)) ) knitr::kable(opt_metrics, digits = 3) plot(LUT_test$Cab, opt_rmse[[2]]$Cab, pch = 19, col = "#2166AC",      xlab = "Observed Cab", ylab = "Predicted Cab (merit-RMSE, nOpt=5)",      main = "LUT merit-function matching") abline(0, 1, col = "grey40", lty = 2)

title: Trait inversion: merit-function matching, ML, and deep learning
text: train/test split, now model actually fit train_df first, applied test_df – per-observation LUT search prediction time:  algorithm = "RF" can swapped get.inversion()’s 12 supported values ("PLSR", "SVM", "GB", "NN", "Bayesian", "AdaBag", "BRNN", "xGB", "RVM", "qLASSO", "Ensemble") – rest call identical.
code: ml_res <- get.inversion(data = train_df, depVar = "Cab", inputs = band_names,                          algorithm = "RF", n.samples = nrow(train_df), seed = 42) pred_ml_test <- as.numeric(predict(ml_res$model, newdata = test_df[, c("Cab", band_names)])) cat("ML (RF)  R2:", round(r2_f(LUT_test$Cab, pred_ml_test), 3),     " RMSE:", round(rmse_f(LUT_test$Cab, pred_ml_test), 3), "\n") #> ML (RF)  R2: 0.715  RMSE: 9.145

what: Why soil matters to a canopy simulation
title: MARMIT + PROSAIL: realistic soil moisture in canopy simulations
text: Top--canopy reflectance mixture leaf optics soil background showing canopy gaps, weighted closed canopy (LAI, leaf angle, hotspot). examples elsewhere package’s docs use fixed, arbitrary rsoil – e.g. 50/50 blend dry wet reference spectrum (--R.Rmd), flat rep(0.15, 2101) (ToolsRTM vignette, InversionOpt.Rmd). ’s fine isolating leaf/canopy trait’s effect, sidesteps real question: much soil’s actual moisture state change sensor sees, depend much vegetation covering ? ToolsRTM::get.marmit.rsoil() (MARMIT: Bablet et al., soil reflectance function surface water film thickness) gives physically-based answer instead arbitrary blend – page feeds output straight foursail()’s rsoil argument.

title: MARMIT + PROSAIL: realistic soil moisture in canopy simulations
text: L (water film thickness, cm) eps (fraction surface ’s wet) control wet simulated soil – Scripts/R/ForMARMIT/1-simulate_LUT.R samples L [0.001, 0.15] eps [0, 1] full LUT; , five fixed steps across range enough see trend:  Soil reflectance darkens broadly wetness (real wet soil looks darker dry soil), strongest relative change SWIR water-absorption region – physics MARMIT built around.
code: wetness_steps <- data.frame(   label = c("Very dry", "Dry", "Moderate", "Wet", "Saturated"),   L     = c(0.001, 0.02, 0.05, 0.09, 0.15),   eps   = c(0.05,  0.3,  0.55, 0.8,  1.0) )  soils <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(wetness_steps)), function(i) {   get.marmit.rsoil(database = "Bablet_2016", id = 1, L = wetness_steps$L[i],                     eps = wetness_steps$eps[i], wl.out = 400:2500) })  cat("Estimated soil moisture (SMC, %) across the sweep:\n") #> Estimated soil moisture (SMC, %) across the sweep: print(round(sapply(soils, function(s) s$SMC), 1)) #> [1]  3.8  9.6 43.6 47.1 47.1 wl <- soils[[1]]$wavelength cols <- colorRampPalette(c("gold", "saddlebrown"))(nrow(wetness_steps)) matplot(wl, sapply(soils, function(s) s$rsoil.wet), type = "l", lty = 1, col = cols,         xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "Soil reflectance",         main = "MARMIT soil reflectance across the wetness sweep") legend("topright", wetness_steps$label, col = cols, lty = 1, cex = 0.8)

what: 2. Feeding it into foursail() at a fixed canopy
title: MARMIT + PROSAIL: realistic soil moisture in canopy simulations
text: leaf/canopy trait set throughout (LAI = 2, moderate canopy), rsoil changes across five wetness steps:  canopy’s spectral shape (chlorophyll absorption, red edge, NIR plateau) stays recognizable throughout – SWIR bands still shift noticeably soil moisture alone, nothing vegetation changed five curves.
code: row <- data.frame(   LAI = 2, hspot = 0.01, LIDFa = -0.35, LIDFb = -0.15, TypeLidf = 1,   tts = 30, tto = 0, psi = 0,   N = 1.5, Cab = 40, Car = 8, Anth = 2, Cbrown = 0, EWT = 0.009, LMA = 0.009, alpha = 40 )  toc_by_soil <- sapply(soils, function(s) {   sail_i <- foursail(inputLUT = row, rsoil = s$rsoil.wet, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")   Compute_BRF(rdot = sail_i$rdot, rsot = sail_i$rsot, tts = row$tts, data.light = dataSpec_PDB) })  matplot(dataSpec_PDB[, 1], toc_by_soil, type = "l", lty = 1, col = cols,         xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "TOC reflectance",         main = "Top-of-canopy reflectance, same canopy, soil wetness varied (LAI=2)") legend("topright", wetness_steps$label, col = cols, lty = 1, cex = 0.8)

what: 3. Does this matter more at low LAI than high LAI?
title: MARMIT + PROSAIL: realistic soil moisture in canopy simulations
text: Physically, yes: sparse canopy leaves soil visible gaps, soil moisture influence sensor-observed signal low LAI high LAI, canopy dominates. Repeat sweep LAI = 0.5 (sparse) LAI = 6 (dense), compare driest-vs-wettest difference SWIR band (1650nm, MARMIT’s strongest water-sensitive region):  sparse canopy’s SWIR reflectance swings much across wetness sweep dense canopy’s – real, physically-expected result, artifact sweep: LAI=6 canopy blocks soil signal regardless wet underneath.
code:
swir_idx <- which(dataSpec_PDB[, 1] == 1650)  toc_by_lai <- function(lai) {   row_i <- row; row_i$LAI <- lai   sapply(soils, function(s) {     sail_i <- foursail(inputLUT = row_i, rsoil = s$rsoil.wet, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")     Compute_BRF(rdot = sail_i$rdot, rsot = sail_i$rsot, tts = row_i$tts, data.light = dataSpec_PDB)[swir_idx]   }) }  refl_sparse <- toc_by_lai(0.5) refl_dense  <- toc_by_lai(6)  cat("SWIR (1650nm) reflectance, driest vs. wettest soil:
") #> SWIR (1650nm) reflectance, driest vs. wettest soil: cat("  Sparse canopy (LAI=0.5): ", round(refl_sparse[1], 4), "->", round(refl_sparse[5], 4),     " (delta =", round(refl_sparse[1] - refl_sparse[5], 4), ")
") #>   Sparse canopy (LAI=0.5):  0.4415 -> 0.0637  (delta = 0.3777 ) cat("  Dense canopy  (LAI=6):   ", round(refl_dense[1], 4),  "->", round(refl_dense[5], 4),     " (delta =", round(refl_dense[1] - refl_dense[5], 4), ")
") #>   Dense canopy  (LAI=6):    0.2134 -> 0.2071  (delta = 0.0064 ) plot(wetness_steps$eps, refl_sparse, type = "o", pch = 19, col = "#B2182B",      ylim = range(c(refl_sparse, refl_dense)),      xlab = "Wetness fraction (eps)", ylab = "TOC reflectance at 1650nm",      main = "Soil-moisture sensitivity shrinks as LAI increases") lines(wetness_steps$eps, refl_dense, type = "o", pch = 19, col = "#2166AC") legend("topright", c("LAI = 0.5 (sparse)", "LAI = 6 (dense)"), col = c("#B2182B", "#2166AC"), pch = 19, lty = 1)

title: MARMIT + PROSAIL: realistic soil moisture in canopy simulations
text: real LUT-based inversion sensitivity study, suggests: target trait canopy structure/LAI, fixed rsoil may fine (soil influence naturally small canopy closes). study covers sparse/senescent vegetation, semi-arid areas, early-season crops – LAI often 1-2 – sample rsoil get.marmit.rsoil() across realistic moisture range (Scripts/R/ForMARMIT/1-simulate_LUT.R) rather fixing , soil moisture variation doesn’t get silently absorbed trait estimates. Scripts/R/Pipeline/0-integrate_MARMIT_soil.R shows get.marmit.rsoil() output wired foursail2(), inform() SPART() well, canopy/TOA models package supports.

title: Model comparison and sensitivity analysis
text: Scripts/Sensibility/ four scripts, answering “traits matter” different method:

title: Model comparison and sensitivity analysis
text: simplest intuitive: vary one trait across realistic range everything else fixed, watch spectrum respond.

what: Global Sobol sensitivity, across the full spectrum
title: Model comparison and sensitivity analysis
text: 1-Sobol_spectral_sensitivity.R uses get.spectral.sensitivity() (wraps get.sobol.indices(), run per wavelength) get global variance-based sensitivity estimate – unlike OAT, every trait varies simultaneously, captures interactions OAT can’t. Run twice, comparing Uniform-PDF sampling scenario Gaussian one:

what: Global Sobol sensitivity, per Sentinel-2A band
title: Model comparison and sensitivity analysis
text: 2-Sobol_perband_sensitivity.R uses sensobol package’s proper quasi-random design (sobol_matrices() → evaluate foursail() every design point → sobol_indices()) get first-order (Si) total (Ti) indices per band, rather per native wavelength:  Structural traits (LAI, LIDFa) dominate NIR/SWIR bands (B6-B8A, B11-B12); pigments (Cab/Car/Anth) dominate visible bands (B2-B5) – exactly leaf/canopy optics theory predicts, useful sanity check whole simulate--estimate pipeline behaving.

title: Model comparison and sensitivity analysis
text: 3-Johnson_relative_importance.R regression-based alternative (sensitivity::johnson()) – doesn’t need special Sobol quasi-random design, ordinary random LUT enough, answers related--different question (relative contribution explained variance, variance decomposition):  Note EWT dominating band B11 (SWIR, classic water-absorption region) – methods agree structural/water traits dominate SWIR pigments dominate visible, reassuring: two different statistical methods converging physical story.

what: A practical note on zero-variance predictors
title: Model comparison and sensitivity analysis
text: Building Scripts/Sensibility/3-Johnson_relative_importance.R surfaced real, generically-useful gotcha: johnson()’s correlation-matrix step fails outright (eigen(): infinite missing values) predictor column zero variance – e.g. LMA constant LUT built LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO", since variant uses CBC/Prot dry matter instead. script now drops zero-variance column calling johnson(), message naming got dropped, rather crashing. Worth checking code time feed LUT-derived data.frame correlation- regression-based method.

what: 1. Leaf traits and canopy structure: one row of parameters
title: 01. Getting Started with ToolsRTM
text: simulation always starts one row trait values – data.frame one column per parameter leaf canopy model need. , PROSPECT-D needs leaf biochemistry (N, Cab, Car, Anth, Cbrown, EWT, LMA); fourSAIL needs canopy structure (LAI, LIDFa/LIDFb/TypeLidf, hspot) sun-view geometry (tts/tto/psi): soil spectrum also required – foursail() mixes leaf optics whatever shows canopy gaps. 50/50 blend package’s bundled dry/wet reference soil spectra reasonable, physically-motivated default (Tutorial 05 covers building LUTs properly; Tutorial 10’s sibling article soil/MARMIT integration covers moisture-realistic alternative):
code: row <- data.frame(   # Canopy structure and geometry (fourSAIL)   LAI = 3, hspot = 0.01, LIDFa = -0.35, LIDFb = -0.15, TypeLidf = 1,   tts = 30, tto = 0, psi = 0,   # Leaf biochemistry (PROSPECT-D)   N = 1.5, Cab = 40, Car = 8, Anth = 2, Cbrown = 0, EWT = 0.009, LMA = 0.009,   alpha = 40 ) rsoil <- 0.5 * dataSpec_PDB[, 11] + 0.5 * dataSpec_PDB[, 12]  # dry/wet soil blend

title: 01. Getting Started with ToolsRTM
text: foursail() runs PROSPECT internally (via LeafModel argument) returns canopy-level outputs directly – ’s need call leaf model minimal example. LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D" selects leaf model; Tutorial 02 shows every leaf model available call PROSPECT leaf-level output needed.

title: 01. Getting Started with ToolsRTM
text: sail$rdot (hemispherical-directional reflectance factor) sail$rsot (bi-directional reflectance factor) fourSAIL’s two raw outputs. Compute_BRF() blends using sun/view geometry single top--canopy (TOC) reflectance spectrum sensor actually observes:
code: sail <- foursail(inputLUT = row, rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D") names(sail) #> [1] "rdot" "rsot" "rddt" "rsdt" reflectance <- Compute_BRF(rdot = sail$rdot, rsot = sail$rsot,                             tts = row$tts, data.light = dataSpec_PDB) length(reflectance)  # one value per nm, 400-2500nm #> [1] 2101

title: 01. Getting Started with ToolsRTM
text: familiar vegetation signature already visible: low reflectance visible (400-700nm, chlorophyll absorption), sharp rise red edge (~700-750nm), high NIR plateau (leaf/canopy structural scattering), two water-absorption dips SWIR (~1450nm, ~1950nm).
code: plot(dataSpec_PDB[, 1], reflectance, type = "l", col = "#2E8B57", lwd = 2,      xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "Reflectance",      main = "One simulation: fourSAIL + PROSPECT-D")

what: 1. Leaf radiative transfer: five models, called standalone
title: 02. From Leaf to Canopy Reflectance
text: ToolsRTM implements five leaf models. Three exported standalone functions (leaf-level , canopy); PROSPECT-D available bundled inside canopy call (foursail(..., LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D"), Section 2 ) – real asymmetry package’s exported API worth knowing rather guessing past.  Liberty (built needle leaves) reads visibly different two broadleaf-oriented models even comparable Cab/EWT – real structural difference, bug, since needle vs. broadleaf internal structure model represents.
code: pro <- prospect_PRO(N = 1.5, Cab = 40, Car = 8, Anth = 2, Cbrown = 0,                      EWT = 0.009, LMA = 0.009, alpha = 40, Prot = 0.002, CBC = 0.007)  lib_row <- data.frame(Cab = 40, EWT = 0.009, lign.cell = 2, Nitrogen = 1,                        cell.d = 40, inter.c = 0.045, baseline.abs = 0.0006,                        leaf.thick = 1.6, albino.abs = 0) lib <- liberty(lib_row)  flu_row <- data.frame(N = 1.8, Cab = 40, Car = 10, Anth = 0, EWT = 0.015,                        LMA = 0.01, Cs = 0.1, fqe = 0.01, Cx = 0, alpha = 40) flu <- getFluspect.B(inputsLeaf = flu_row, inputsOptipar = ToolsRTM::optipar, version = "D")  plot(pro$lambda, pro$refl, type = "l", col = "#0072B2", lwd = 2, ylim = c(0, 0.6),      xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "Leaf reflectance",      main = "Leaf reflectance: three models, similar Cab/EWT") lines(lib$lambda, lib$refl, col = "#009E73", lwd = 2) lines(flu$lambda, flu$refl, col = "#D55E00", lwd = 2) legend("topright", c("PROSPECT-PRO", "Liberty", "Fluspect-B"),        col = c("#0072B2", "#009E73", "#D55E00"), lwd = 2)

title: 02. From Leaf to Canopy Reflectance
text: fourSAIL, fourSAIL2, INFORM take kind leaf reflectance/transmittance turn canopy-level BRF, differ canopy structure represent – , correspondingly, extra parameters LUT needs: inform()’s return shape (bare vector, list(rdot=, rsot=)) real, useful--know inconsistency across three canopy functions – simulate_RTM() (used later tutorials) normalizes away, raw functions used directly .  INFORM’s forest-level reflectance sits visibly lower fourSAIL’s – expected, since INFORM’s explicit crown/shadow geometry isn’t present fourSAIL’s turbid-medium assumption. Tutorial 04 makes comparison systematic (5 leaf models x 3 canopy models, plus agreement/RMSE table); page mechanism, survey.
code: common_lut <- data.frame(   N = 1.5, Cab = 40, Car = 8, Anth = 1, Cbrown = 0, EWT = 0.01, LMA = 0.009, alpha = 40,   Prot = 0.002, CBC = 0.007, Cs = 0, fqe = 0.01, Cx = 0,   cell.d = 40, inter.c = 0.045, baseline.abs = 0.0006, leaf.thick = 1.6,   albino.abs = 0, lign.cell = 2, Nitrogen = 1,   LIDFa = -0.35, LIDFb = -0.15, TypeLidf = 1, LAI = 3, hspot = 0.01,   tts = 30, tto = 0, psi = 0,   fraction_brown = 0.1, diss = 0.5, Cv = 1, Zeta = 0,   LAIu = 0.5, sd = 650, cd = 4.5, h = 20, skyl = 0.1 ) rsoil <- rep(0.15, 2101) wl <- 400:2500  sim_foursail  <- foursail(inputLUT = common_lut, rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")$rsot sim_foursail2 <- foursail2(inputLUT = common_lut, rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")$rsot sim_inform    <- inform(inputLUT = common_lut, rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")  # bare vector  plot(wl, sim_foursail, type = "l", col = "#0072B2", lwd = 2, ylim = c(0, 0.5),      xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "TOC reflectance (rsot)",      main = "Canopy models: same LUT, same leaf model (PROSPECT-D)") lines(wl, sim_foursail2, col = "#009E73", lwd = 2) lines(wl, sim_inform, col = "#D55E00", lwd = 2) legend("topright", c("fourSAIL", "fourSAIL2", "INFORM"),        col = c("#0072B2", "#009E73", "#D55E00"), lwd = 2)

what: 3. How trait changes propagate: leaf sweeps that reach the canopy
title: 02. From Leaf to Canopy Reflectance
text: Sweep Cab EWT one time (everything else fixed) watch canopy-level spectrum respond – leaf--canopy chain preserves trait’s spectral signature, just attenuated/reshaped canopy:  trait leaves signature different spectral region – Cab visible/red-edge (chlorophyll absorption), EWT SWIR (water absorption), LAI mainly NIR plateau height (leaf layers, multiple scattering) visible saturates quickly canopy closed enough hide soil. Tutorial 10 formalizes proper global sensitivity analysis (Sobol/Johnson indices) rather one-trait---time sweeps.
code: sweep_trait <- function(trait, values) {   sapply(values, function(v) {     row2 <- common_lut; row2[[trait]] <- v     foursail(inputLUT = row2, rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")$rsot   }) } cab_curves <- sweep_trait("Cab", seq(10, 70, length.out = 6)) ewt_curves <- sweep_trait("EWT", seq(0.005, 0.03, length.out = 6)) lai_curves <- sweep_trait("LAI", seq(0.5, 7, length.out = 6))  op <- par(mfrow = c(3, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)) matplot(wl, cab_curves, type = "l", lty = 1, col = colorRampPalette(c("gold", "darkgreen"))(6),         xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "rsot", main = "Sweeping Cab (10-70 ug/cm2): visible/red-edge") matplot(wl, ewt_curves, type = "l", lty = 1, col = colorRampPalette(c("gold", "darkblue"))(6),         xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "rsot", main = "Sweeping EWT (0.005-0.03 g/cm2): SWIR") matplot(wl, lai_curves, type = "l", lty = 1, col = colorRampPalette(c("gold", "firebrick"))(6),         xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "rsot", main = "Sweeping LAI (0.5-7): NIR plateau + visible saturation") par(op)

title: 03. SPART: Soil-Plant-Atmosphere Radiative Transfer
text: Inputs fall five physical domains. inputsSPART (getLUT()-ready table, pattern inputsPROSAIL) already groups : Full argument documentation lives ?SPART – page focuses pieces fit together, exhaustive parameter list.
code: LUT <- as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = ToolsRTM::inputsSPART, nLUT = 5, setseed = 1)) # inputsSPART only ships PROSPECT-PRO/-D columns -- add what other leaf # models need too (same requirement as foursail()/SPART() itself). LUT$Cs <- 0; LUT$fqe <- 0.01; LUT$Cx <- 0 LUT$cell.d <- 40; LUT$inter.c <- 0.045; LUT$baseline.abs <- 0.0006 LUT$leaf.thick <- 1.6; LUT$albino.abs <- 0; LUT$lign.cell <- 2; LUT$Nitrogen <- 1 # A realistic, sea-level, clear-sky atmosphere for the worked example below # (getLUT()'s own default sampling range for the atmosphere columns is wide # enough to occasionally draw physically implausible combinations -- see # the note at the end of Section 3.2). title: 03. SPART: Soil-Plant-Atmosphere Radiative Transfer
text: Unlike foursail(), SPART returns output already convolved chosen sensor’s bands (sensor.) – separate “simulate native, convolve” step (Tutorial 07 covers convolution foursail()/inform() output, stays 1nm resolution).   dip near 942nm near-total collapse near 1372nm real atmospheric water-vapour absorption bands – present TOA curve absent TOC, exactly real atmospheric correction deal ; diff plot makes quantitative: atmosphere adds reflectance visible (positive ΔRatm\Delta R_{atm}, mostly Rayleigh/ aerosol path radiance) removes water-vapour/near-infrared bands (negative ΔRatm\Delta R_{atm}, absorption), rather shifting whole spectrum uniformly. note getLUT()’s atmosphere sampling: wide default ranges inputsSPART samples , random rows combine high aot550 (aerosol loading) high alt_m (altitude) – combination SMAC’s atmospheric correction doesn’t handle gracefully, producing negative (physically meaningless) TOA reflectance. Always sanity-check range(sim$output$rfl.toa) random draw; fixed, realistic sea-level clear-sky atmosphere set Section 3.1 avoids rest page.
code: sim <- suppressWarnings(SPART(inputLUT = LUT[1, ], CanopyModel = "fourSAIL",                                LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO",                                sensor.i = ToolsRTM::Sentinel2A.MSI,                                rsoil = NULL, get.plots = FALSE)) names(sim$output)  # wave, rad.toa, rfl.toa, rfl.toc, rfl.toc.BRDF -- already at Sentinel-2A's own bands #> [1] "wave"         "rad.toa"      "rfl.toa"      "rfl.toc"      "rfl.toc.BRDF" plot(sim$output$wave, sim$output$rfl.toc.BRDF, type = "o", pch = 19, col = "#0072B2",      ylim = c(0, max(sim$output$rfl.toc.BRDF, sim$output$rfl.toa)),      xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "Reflectance", main = "SPART: TOC vs. TOA (Sentinel-2A bands)") lines(sim$output$wave, sim$output$rfl.toa, type = "o", pch = 19, col = "#D55E00") legend("topright", c("TOC (canopy)", "TOA (satellite)"), col = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00"), pch = 19, lty = 1) diff_atm <- sim$output$rfl.toa - sim$output$rfl.toc.BRDF plot(sim$output$wave, diff_atm, type = "o", pch = 19, col = "#CC79A7",      xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = expression(Delta*R[atm] == R[TOA] - R[TOC]),      main = "Atmospheric contribution: TOA minus TOC") abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "grey50")

SPART() used hardcode four internally (BSMBrightness = 0.5, BSMlat = 25, BSMlon = 45, SMp = 15) regardless LUT. now fixed: SPART() reads four columns inputLUT present (falling back defaults otherwise, old code unaffected), inputsSPART now ships four real, sampleable parameters.

what: A sensitivity test showing each BSM parameter’s real effect
title: 03. SPART: Soil-Plant-Atmosphere Radiative Transfer
text: four now real, verifiable effect – brighter soil (BSMBrightness) drier soil (lower SMp) raise reflectance, expected; BSMlat/BSMlon reshape soil spectrum’s spectral shape rather overall level, effect single band smaller still real.
code: run1 <- function(row) suppressWarnings(SPART(inputLUT = row, CanopyModel = "fourSAIL", LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO",                                               sensor.i = ToolsRTM::Sentinel2A.MSI, rsoil = NULL, get.plots = FALSE)) base_row <- LUT[1, ]; base_row$LAI <- 1  # sparse-ish canopy so soil shows through bsm_params <- list(BSMBrightness = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8), BSMlat = c(20, 25, 40),                     BSMlon = c(45, 45, 65), SMp = c(5, 15, 55)) cat("NIR band (789nm) TOC reflectance as each BSM parameter varies (others at their default):\n") #> NIR band (789nm) TOC reflectance as each BSM parameter varies (others at their default): for (p in names(bsm_params)) {   vals <- bsm_params[[p]]   outs <- sapply(vals, function(v) { r <- base_row; r[[p]] <- v; run1(r)$output$rfl.toc.BRDF[8] })   cat(sprintf("  %-14s %s -> %s\n", p, paste(vals, collapse = " / "), paste(round(outs, 4), collapse = " / "))) } #>   BSMBrightness  0.2 / 0.5 / 0.8 -> 0.2487 / 0.353 / 0.476 #>   BSMlat         20 / 25 / 40 -> 0.3268 / 0.353 / 0.4277 #>   BSMlon         45 / 45 / 65 -> 0.353 / 0.353 / 0.3671 #>   SMp            5 / 15 / 55 -> 0.3039 / 0.353 / 0.2529

title: 03. SPART: Soil-Plant-Atmosphere Radiative Transfer
text: Section 3.2’s TOA-TOC diff plot showed atmosphere’s total effect. atmospheric variable drives , spectrum, varies lot: aot550 (aerosol loading) shifts mainly visible bands (445-654nm, rising aerosol – path radiance/scattering); uh2o (water vapour) almost invisible outside two water-absorption bands (942nm, 1372nm) dominates completely; uo3 (ozone)’s effect small concentrated around 560nm (Chappuis band). Different gases, different spectral fingerprints – single “atmosphere /” comparison (Section 3.2) can’t show , per-driver sweep can.

title: 03. SPART: Soil-Plant-Atmosphere Radiative Transfer
text: tts (sun zenith), tto (view zenith), psi (relative azimuth) feed fourSAIL’s BRDF term inside SPART, way Compute_BRF() (Tutorial 01) – makes reflectance direction-dependent rather single fixed number per surface. inputsSPART fixes tts = 0 default (sun straight overhead), simple geometric symmetry makes psi irrelevant (’s “relative” direction sun azimuth ) – section fixes tts = 30 instead, specifically let tto psi show real effect: real BRDF effects: moving psi away 0 deg (away sun’s azimuth, .e. away backscatter/hotspot direction) lowers NIR reflectance ; increasing tto toward tts (staying backscatter direction, psi=0) raises , approaching hotspot. specific direction (higher tto -> higher reflectance) property geometry configuration (backscatter side, psi=0, LAI/LIDF), general rule – forward-scatter side (psi near 180) tto increase can lower reflectance instead. Lambertian (direction-independent) assumption miss .
