what: 3.7 Why the TOC/TOA distinction matters for inversion
title: 03. SPART: Soil-Plant-Atmosphere Radiative Transfer
text: SPART slots hybrid-inversion framework rest series builds (Tutorials 10-13) – reflectance domain model trained matters enormously, real satellite data always TOA, never TOC: ’s small effect: Cab-inversion model trained TOC reflectance (incorrectly) applied TOA reflectance real satellite collapses negative R² – worse just predicting mean every time – model trained TOA reflectance first place performs well -atmosphere ideal. concrete, load-bearing reason SPART() exists package: LUT built plain foursail()/inform() training inversion model later see real satellite reflectance needs either atmospheric-correction step real data, – SPART() provides directly – LUT simulated way TOA first place. developed (train/test mechanics Tutorial 11’s job) – section exists make reason concrete tutorial’s worked example.
code: LUT150 <- as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = ToolsRTM::inputsSPART, nLUT = 150, setseed = 1)) # Fix only atmosphere/BSM-soil (a realistic single-scene assumption, same as the # rest of this page) -- leaf/canopy traits vary naturally across all 150 rows, # same as a real inversion LUT (Tutorials 11-12). Fixing every non-Cab column # (an earlier version of this chunk did) leaves only one varying predictor # against 13 highly collinear bands -- a degenerate, overfit regression, not a # realistic inversion. for (col in c("Pa", "aot550", "uo3", "uh2o", "alt_m", "Pa0", "BSMBrightness", "BSMlat", "BSMlon", "SMp")) {   LUT150[[col]] <- LUT[[col]][1] }  sims <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(LUT150)), function(i) run1(LUT150[i, ])) toc_mat <- t(sapply(sims, function(s) s$output$rfl.toc.BRDF)) toa_mat <- t(sapply(sims, function(s) s$output$rfl.toa)) colnames(toc_mat) <- colnames(toa_mat) <- paste0("B", seq_len(ncol(toc_mat)))  set.seed(1) train_idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(LUT150)), size = round(0.7 * nrow(LUT150))) test_idx <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(LUT150)), train_idx) cab <- LUT150$Cab  fit_toc <- lm(cab[train_idx] ~ ., data = as.data.frame(toc_mat[train_idx, ])) fit_toa <- lm(cab[train_idx] ~ ., data = as.data.frame(toa_mat[train_idx, ]))  r2 <- function(y, p) 1 - sum((y - p)^2) / sum((y - mean(y))^2) rmse <- function(y, p) sqrt(mean((y - p)^2)) truth <- cab[test_idx]  pred_ideal <- predict(fit_toc, newdata = as.data.frame(toc_mat[test_idx, ]))     # TOC model, TOC data pred_correct <- predict(fit_toa, newdata = as.data.frame(toa_mat[test_idx, ]))   # TOA model, TOA data pred_domaingap <- predict(fit_toc, newdata = as.data.frame(toa_mat[test_idx, ])) # TOC model misapplied to TOA data  data.frame(   scenario = c("TOC-trained model on TOC data (best case, no atmosphere)",                "TOA-trained model on TOA data (correct real-world approach)",                "TOC-trained model applied to TOA data (the domain-gap mistake)"),   R2 = round(c(r2(truth, pred_ideal), r2(truth, pred_correct), r2(truth, pred_domaingap)), 3),   RMSE = round(c(rmse(truth, pred_ideal), rmse(truth, pred_correct), rmse(truth, pred_domaingap)), 2) ) |> knitr::kable() Parameter LUT      |      v SPART simulations (already at sensor bands, TOC or TOA)      |      v Synthetic EO training dataset -- must match what you'll invert later      |      v ML inversion      |      v Vegetation traits

text: Every leaf model x every canopy model supports , plus deviation--ensemble-mean heatmap – white means models agree wavelength, saturated colour means diverge:
code: df_grid <- bind_rows(lapply(canopy_models, function(cm) {   bind_rows(lapply(leaf_models, function(lm) {     short_domain <- lm %in% c("Fluspect-B", "Fluspect-B-Cx")     rsoil <- if (short_domain && cm != "INFORM") rsoil_2001 else rsoil_2101     sim <- tryCatch({       if (cm == "fourSAIL") foursail(inputLUT = common_lut, rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = lm, spectrum.all = !short_domain)$rsot       else if (cm == "foursail2") foursail2(inputLUT = common_lut, rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = lm)$rsot       else inform(inputLUT = common_lut, rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = lm)     }, error = function(e) NULL)     if (is.null(sim)) return(NULL)     data.frame(wavelength = if (short_domain) wl_2001 else wl_2101, rsot = sim, leaf_model = lm, canopy_model = cm)   })) })) df_grid$combo <- paste(df_grid$canopy_model, df_grid$leaf_model, sep = " + ")  ggplot(df_grid, aes(x = wavelength, y = rsot, color = leaf_model)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) + facet_wrap(~canopy_model) + scale_color_manual(values = leaf_colors) +   labs(title = "All canopy models x all leaf models", x = "Wavelength (nm)",        y = "TOC reflectance (rsot)", color = "Leaf model") + theme_rtm df_common <- df_grid[df_grid$wavelength <= 2400, ] %>%   group_by(wavelength) %>% mutate(ensemble_mean = mean(rsot), deviation = rsot - ensemble_mean) %>% ungroup()  ggplot(df_common, aes(x = wavelength, y = combo, fill = deviation)) +   geom_raster() +   scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", midpoint = 0, name = "rsot - mean") +   labs(title = "Where models agree and where they don't", x = "Wavelength (nm)", y = NULL) +   theme_rtm + theme(legend.position = "right", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))

what: 2. get_distributionLUT(): a different distribution per trait
title: 05. Building Look-Up Tables
text: Real leaf/canopy traits don’t follow distribution shape. Chlorophyll content (Cab) tends cluster around typical value (Gaussian-like); leaf-angle parameter LIDFa tendency across mixed canopy (closer Uniform). get_distributionLUT() lets trait pick shape instead forcing one distribution .  Cab (Gaussian) LIDFa (Uniform) came exact call – histograms show picking right distribution per trait matters.
code: minval <- data.frame('N' = 1.5, 'Cab' = 5, 'Car' = 0, 'Anth' = 0, 'Cbrown' = 0.0,                       'EWT' = 0.001, 'Prot' = 0.00001, 'CBC' = 0.00001,                       'LIDFa' = 0, 'LAI' = 0.5,                       LAIu = 0, sd = 200, cd = 0.2, h = 5,                       fraction_brown = 0, diss = 0.1, Cv = 0.3, Zeta = 0) maxval <- data.frame('N' = 3, 'Cab' = 70, 'Car' = 25, 'Anth' = 7, 'Cbrown' = 0.2,                       'EWT' = 0.035, 'Prot' = 0.03, 'CBC' = 0.03,                       'LIDFa' = 70, 'LAI' = 7,                       LAIu = 0.8, sd = 1000, cd = 7, h = 20,                       fraction_brown = 1, diss = 1, Cv = 1, Zeta = 0.2) TypeDistrib <- data.frame('N' = 'Gaussian', 'Cab' = 'Gaussian', 'Car' = 'Gaussian',                            'Anth' = 'Uniform', 'Cbrown' = 'Uniform',                            'EWT' = 'Uniform', 'Prot' = 'Uniform', 'CBC' = 'Uniform',                            'LIDFa' = 'Uniform', 'LAI' = 'Gaussian',                            LAIu = 'Uniform', sd = 'Uniform', cd = 'Uniform', h = 'Uniform',                            fraction_brown = 'Uniform', diss = 'Uniform', Cv = 'Uniform', Zeta = 'Uniform') Mean_gauss <- data.frame('N' = 2.2, 'Cab' = 45, 'Car' = 8, 'LAI' = 2.25) std_gauss <- Mean_gauss / 2.0  data.LUT <- get_distributionLUT(minval = minval, maxval = maxval, nSamples = 500,                                  TypeDistrib = TypeDistrib, Mean_gauss = Mean_gauss,                                  Std_gauss = std_gauss, DepCab = FALSE, setseed = 246) op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) hist(data.LUT$Cab, breaks = 30, col = "#2E8B57", border = "white",      main = "Cab (Gaussian, mean=45)", xlab = "Cab") hist(data.LUT$LIDFa, breaks = 30, col = "#B2182B", border = "white",      main = "LIDFa (Uniform)", xlab = "LIDFa") par(op)

title: 06. Large-Scale and Parallel RTM Simulation
text: Three things matter pattern actually work, just look parallel: makeCluster()/registerDoParallel()/stopCluster() always paired – unclosed cluster leaks worker processes across whole R session, compounding chunk runs (e.g. re-knitting interactively). .packages = "ToolsRTM" inside foreach() – worker process starts fresh, packages attached; without , foursail() isn’t found workers every iteration errors. no_cores <- detectCores() - 2, detectCores() – leaves headroom OS R session’s main process, convention package’s course scripts (ForPROSAIL, Sensibility) use throughout.
code: no_cores <- max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 2) # CRAN check machines cap parallel workers at 2; respect that limit so this # vignette rebuilds cleanly under R CMD check --as-cran. if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("_R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_"))) no_cores <- min(no_cores, 2L) cl <- makeCluster(no_cores) registerDoParallel(cl)  t_par <- system.time({   sims_par <- foreach(i = 1:n.samples, .packages = "ToolsRTM") %dopar% {     sail_i <- foursail(inputLUT = LUT[i, ], rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")     sail_i$rsot   } }) stopCluster(cl)  cat("Parallel (", no_cores, "cores):", round(t_par[["elapsed"]], 2), "s for", n.samples, "simulations\n") #> Parallel ( 10 cores): 5.14 s for 300 simulations cat("Speedup:", round(t_seq[["elapsed"]] / t_par[["elapsed"]], 2), "x\n") #> Speedup: 1.65 x identical(sims_seq[[1]], sims_par[[1]])  # same result, sequential or parallel #> [1] TRUE

code: headwall_step <- 400.247 - 398.0166 cat("Confirmed real step size from the 5-value header snippet:", round(headwall_step, 4), "nm\n") #> Confirmed real step size from the 5-value header snippet: 2.2304 nm  # Extrapolating the real header's own documented step to its full stated # length (272 bands) -- not a fabricated instrument, the real spacing # applied for its full real extent. headwall_vnir_centers <- 398.0166 + (0:271) * headwall_step cat("VNIR range:", round(range(headwall_vnir_centers), 1), "nm,", length(headwall_vnir_centers), "bands\n") #> VNIR range: 398 1002.5 nm, 272 bands  headwall_vnir_bands <- get.spectral.convolution.gaussian(df, centers = headwall_vnir_centers) plot(df$wave, df$rfl, type = "l", col = "grey70",      xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "Reflectance", main = "Headwall Nano-Hyperspec VNIR (272 bands, centers only)") # Points, not a solid line -- at 272 bands / 2.23nm spacing a solid line is # dense enough to fully cover the native grey line underneath; points let # the native spectrum show through between them. Same green used for the # hyperspectral/dense-sensor overlay throughout this page (Sections 2-4). points(headwall_vnir_bands$wl, headwall_vnir_bands$RFL, col = "#2E8B57", pch = 19, cex = 0.8) legend("topright", c("Native 1nm", "Headwall VNIR"), col = c("grey70", "#2E8B57"), lty = c(1, NA), pch = c(NA, 19))

what: 6. Spectral sampling density, side by side
title: 08. Hyperspectral and VNIR Sensor Convolution
text: Approx_spacing_nm NA two irregular/mixed-sampling rows – 15-band rig places bands specific absorption features rather uniform steps, illustrative VNIR+SWIR row mixes real 2.23nm VNIR step representative 5nm SWIR step, single averaged number misrepresent .  “hyperspectral” buys multispectral, concretely: Sentinel-2A’s 13 bands can sample absorption features red-edge shape handful fixed points; PRISMA/EnMAP/Headwall’s 200+ narrow bands resolve actual continuous shape features – difference lets hyperspectral data support things multispectral can’t (e.g. narrowband indices centered exactly absorption feature, fitting absorption-feature depth/position directly rather inferring handful wide bands).
code: comparison <- data.frame(   Sensor = c("Sentinel-2A", "PRISMA", "EnMAP", "Own 15-band rig", "Headwall VNIR", "Headwall VNIR+SWIR (illustrative)"),   Bands = c(nrow(se2_bands), nrow(prisma_bands), nrow(enmap_bands),             nrow(own_bands), nrow(headwall_vnir_bands), nrow(headwall_vnirswir_bands)),   Approx_spacing_nm = c(round(diff(range(se2_bands$wl)) / (nrow(se2_bands) - 1), 0),                          round(diff(range(prisma_bands$wl)) / (nrow(prisma_bands) - 1), 1),                          round(diff(range(enmap_bands$wl)) / (nrow(enmap_bands) - 1), 1),                          NA,                          round(headwall_step, 2),                          NA) ) knitr::kable(comparison) op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)) plot(df$wave, df$rfl, type = "l", col = "grey70", ylim = c(0, max(df$rfl)),      xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "Reflectance", main = "Multispectral: Sentinel-2A (13 bands)") points(se2_bands$wl, se2_bands$RFL, col = "#B2182B", pch = 19) plot(df$wave, df$rfl, type = "l", col = "grey70", ylim = c(0, max(df$rfl)),      xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "Reflectance", main = "Hyperspectral: PRISMA (dense) vs. Headwall VNIR (272 bands)") lines(prisma_bands$wl, prisma_bands$RFL, col = "#2E8B57", lwd = 1) points(headwall_vnir_bands$wl, headwall_vnir_bands$RFL, col = "#E31A1C", pch = ".", cex = 2) legend("topright", c("PRISMA", "Headwall VNIR"), col = c("#2E8B57", "#E31A1C"), lty = 1, cex = 0.8) par(op)

what: 1. Global sensitivity across the full spectrum: Johnson relative importance
title: 10. Understanding RTM Sensitivity
text: get.spectral.sensitivity() runs sensitivity::johnson() (Johnson relative-importance index) per wavelength – every trait varies simultaneously per simulation, unlike Tutorial 02’s OAT sweeps. real bug found fixed building page: function’s name earlier draft page said “Sobol total index” – get.sobol.indices() (get.spectral.sensitivity() calls internally) compute Sobol total index (STi), specific column genuine formula bug (accidentally squares output instead using input trait , every trait came nearly value – telltale symptom Cab, EWT, LAI landing within percentage point every wavelength, including right next 400 vs 410nm, physical reason flat). Fixed switching get.sobol.indices()’s separately, correctly computed .Johnson_norm column (sensitivity::johnson(), different code path function) – metric package’s reference sensitivity scripts already use exact kind figure. STi_pct column name kept backward compatibility even though Johnson-based now, Sobol-based.  number lands exactly leaf/canopy optics theory says – Cab visible, EWT water bands, LAI NIR – concrete confirmation fix produced real physics, another plausible-looking wrong pattern. Cab dominates visible, EWT SWIR water-absorption region – consistent Tutorial 02’s OAT sweeps, now every trait varying jointly rather one time.

what: 2. Global Sobol sensitivity, per Sentinel-2A band
title: 10. Understanding RTM Sensitivity
text: proper quasi-random Sobol design (sensobol::sobol_matrices()), giving first-order (Si) total (Ti) indices per band rather per native wavelength:  LAI dominates NIR band (B8); pigments (Cab/Car) dominate red band (B4) – exactly leaf/canopy optics theory predicts.
code: library(sensobol) params <- c("Cab", "Car", "LAI", "EWT") N <- 40  # base sample size; total simulations = N * (length(params) + 2) mat01 <- sobol_matrices(N = N, params = params) ranges <- list(Cab = c(5, 90), Car = c(0.5, 25), LAI = c(0.5, 7), EWT = c(0.001, 0.035))  LUT_sobol <- as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL, nLUT = nrow(mat01), setseed = 1234)) for (p in params) LUT_sobol[[p]] <- ranges[[p]][1] + mat01[, p] * diff(ranges[[p]]) # inputsPROSAIL's own LMA row is held fixed at 0 by design (getLUT() samples # Prot/CBC instead, PROSPECT-PRO's dry-matter inputs) -- LeafModel="PROSPECT-D" # below needs LMA directly, so sample it from a typical real-leaf range. set.seed(1235) LUT_sobol$LMA <- runif(nrow(LUT_sobol), 0.005, 0.02)  rsoil <- rep(0.15, 2101) refl <- t(sapply(seq_len(nrow(LUT_sobol)), function(i) {   foursail(inputLUT = LUT_sobol[i, ], rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")$rsot })) colnames(refl) <- paste0("R.", 400:2500) refl_X <- as.data.frame(refl); colnames(refl_X) <- paste0("X", 400:2500); refl_X <- cbind(id = seq_len(nrow(refl_X)), refl_X) se2a <- suppressMessages(get.spectra.convolved(rfl = refl_X, sensor = "Sentinel2a", plot.spectra = FALSE)) #> [1] "Spectral resampling function to SENTINEL2A is being processed ..." #>   |                                                                              | lapply(c("B4", "B8", "B11"), function(band) {   ind <- sobol_indices(Y = se2a[[band]], N = N, params = params)   data.frame(Band = band, Parameter = ind$results$parameters, Index = ind$results$original, Type = ind$results$sensitivity) })) ggplot(subset(sobol_df, Type == "Ti"), aes(x = Band, y = Index, fill = Parameter)) +   geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") + what: A practical note on zero-variance predictors
title: 10. Understanding RTM Sensitivity
text: Building Johnson section surfaced real, generically-useful gotcha: johnson()’s correlation-matrix step fails outright (eigen(): infinite missing values) predictor column zero variance – e.g. LMA constant LUT built LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO", since variant uses CBC/Prot dry matter instead. Always check drop constant columns feeding LUT-derived data.frame correlation- regression-based sensitivity method.

title: 14. End-to-End RTM Inversion Pipeline
text: simulate_RTM() dispatches foursail()/foursail2()/inform() based canopy.model – canopy.model single variable, separate script per model:
code: run_pipeline <- function(canopy.model, leaf.model = "PROSPECT-D", n.samples = 500, seed = 1) {   LUT <- as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL, nLUT = n.samples, setseed = seed))   # inputsPROSAIL's own LMA row is held fixed at 0 by design (getLUT() samples   # Prot/CBC instead, PROSPECT-PRO's dry-matter inputs) -- the default   # leaf.model="PROSPECT-D" needs LMA directly, so sample it here from a   # typical real-leaf range; ignored (harmless) for other leaf models.   LUT$LMA <- stats::runif(n.samples, 0.005, 0.02)   LUT$Cs <- 0; LUT$fqe <- 0.01; LUT$Cx <- 0   LUT$cell.d <- 40; LUT$inter.c <- 0.045; LUT$baseline.abs <- 0.0006   LUT$leaf.thick <- 1.6; LUT$albino.abs <- 0; LUT$lign.cell <- 2; LUT$Nitrogen <- 1   LUT$fraction_brown <- 0.1; LUT$diss <- 0.5; LUT$Cv <- 1; LUT$Zeta <- 0   LUT$LAIu <- 0.5; LUT$sd <- 650; LUT$cd <- 4.5; LUT$h <- 20; LUT$skyl <- 0.1    rsoil <- rep(0.15, 2101)   # 500 simulations per canopy model, x3 models -- parallelized the same way   # as Tutorial 06, rather than a plain sapply(), to keep this vignette's   # build time reasonable at this sample size.   no_cores <- max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 2)   cl <- makeCluster(no_cores)   registerDoParallel(cl)   refl_list <- foreach(i = seq_len(n.samples), .packages = "ToolsRTM") %dopar% {     suppressMessages(simulate_RTM(inputLUT = LUT[i, ], rsoil = rsoil,                                    leaf.model = leaf.model, canopy.model = canopy.model))$rsot   }   stopCluster(cl)   refl <- do.call(rbind, refl_list)   colnames(refl) <- paste0("R.", 400:2500)    refl_X <- as.data.frame(refl); colnames(refl_X) <- paste0("X", 400:2500); refl_X <- cbind(id = seq_len(n.samples), refl_X)   se2a <- suppressMessages(get.spectra.convolved(rfl = refl_X, sensor = "Sentinel2a", plot.spectra = FALSE))   band_names <- paste0("B", seq_along(as.numeric(names(se2a)[-1])))   names(se2a) <- c("id", band_names)    train_idx <- sample(seq_len(n.samples), size = round(0.7 * n.samples))   train_df <- cbind(LUT[train_idx, ], se2a[train_idx, band_names])   test_df  <- cbind(LUT[-train_idx, ], se2a[-train_idx, band_names])    fit <- get.inversion(data = train_df, depVar = "LAI", inputs = band_names,                         algorithm = "RF", n.samples = nrow(train_df), seed = 42)   pred <- as.numeric(predict(fit$model, newdata = test_df[, c("LAI", band_names)]))   r2 <- 1 - sum((test_df$LAI - pred)^2) / sum((test_df$LAI - mean(test_df$LAI))^2)    list(LUT = LUT, refl = refl, obs = test_df$LAI, pred = pred, r2 = r2) }

code: retrieval <- tryCatch({   library(sf)   # Wageningen, NL -- open farmland, a plausible study area for this package   pt <- st_point(c(5.6667, 51.9667)) |> st_sfc(crs = 4326)   scenario <- st_as_sf(data.frame(id = 1), geometry = st_sfc(pt[[1]], crs = 4326))    sc <- get.satellite_collection(scenario = scenario, collection = "sentinel-2-l2a",                                   cloud_server = "microsoft", n.limit = 20,                                   date_range = c("2024-06-01", "2024-08-31"),                                   cloud_threshold = 20, buffer_size = 1500)    bbox <- get_bounding_box(scenario, 1500)   shape <- st_as_sf(data.frame(id = 1), geometry = st_sfc(st_polygon(list(rbind(     c(bbox["xmin"], bbox["ymin"]), c(bbox["xmin"], bbox["ymax"]),     c(bbox["xmax"], bbox["ymax"]), c(bbox["xmax"], bbox["ymin"]),     c(bbox["xmin"], bbox["ymin"])))), crs = 4326))    cube <- get.sentinel2_cube(sc[[1]], shape = shape, date_range = c("2024-06-01", "2024-08-31"),                               aggregation_method = "mean", get.dataset = FALSE)   # Real sun geometry for this acquisition, from the STAC item's own metadata   # (df.data -- the second element get.satellite_collection() returns) --   # used below to build a more realistic training LUT instead of a default   # fixed angle.   df_meta <- sc[[2]]   list(ok = TRUE, cube = cube, df_meta = df_meta) }, error = function(e) list(ok = FALSE, msg = conditionMessage(e)))  if (!retrieval$ok) {   cat("STAC retrieval skipped -- no network/STAC access from this build environment (",       retrieval$msg, "). Everything below needs `retrieval$cube` and is skipped too.\n") } if (retrieval$ok) {   cube <- retrieval$cube   cat("Real Sentinel-2 cube retrieved:", paste(dim(cube), collapse = " x "),       "(rows x cols x bands), bands:", paste(names(cube), collapse = ", "), "\n") } #> Real Sentinel-2 cube retrieved: 161 x 161 x 11 (rows x cols x bands), bands: B02, B03, B04, B05, B06, B07, B08, B8A, B11, B12, SCL

what: 2. A vegetation mask, before any inversion
title: 15. From Satellite Reflectance to Vegetation Traits: Real EO Application
text: Inverting trait model every pixel – bare soil, roads, water – produces number , number meaningless outside vegetation. Build apply NDVI-based mask first:
code: if (retrieval$ok) {   refl_cube <- cube[[c("B02","B03","B04","B05","B06","B07","B08","B8A","B11","B12")]] / 10000   ndvi <- (refl_cube[["B08"]] - refl_cube[["B04"]]) / (refl_cube[["B08"]] + refl_cube[["B04"]])   names(ndvi) <- "NDVI"    # NDVI > 0.3 is a common, but application-dependent, vegetation threshold   # (dense crops/forest often clear 0.5+; this is deliberately permissive   # enough to include sparser/early-season vegetation too). A real   # operational workflow would tune this per land-cover context, and could   # combine it with the cube's own SCL classes for a stricter mask.   veg_mask <- ndvi > 0.3    op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))   plot(ndvi, main = "NDVI (cloud-masked mean composite)")   plot(veg_mask, main = "Vegetation mask (NDVI > 0.3)", col = c("grey85", "#009E73"))   par(op)   cat("Vegetation pixels:", round(100 * sum(values(veg_mask), na.rm = TRUE) / sum(!is.na(values(veg_mask))), 1), "% of the scene\n") } #> Vegetation pixels: 64 % of the scene

what: 3. A realistic, sufficiently large training LUT
title: 15. From Satellite Reflectance to Vegetation Traits: Real EO Application
text: n_samples = 150 (page’s previous size) demo size, scientific one – size alone isn’t whole story either. larger better-constrained LUT can improve inversion providing denser coverage relevant parameter space; automatically improve inversion just larger (100,000 badly- parameterized simulations can worse 5,000 well-designed ones). LUT improves three fronts , just row count: Real acquisition geometry: sun zenith scene’s STAC metadata, package’s generic fixed default. Variable soil, one flat rsoil = 0.15 every row – sampled brightness across realistic range (Tutorial 03’s BSM sensitivity section covers physics). larger sample count – 2000 rows (150), largest practical page’s build time; Section 4 shows explicitly specific number defensible, arbitrary.
code: if (retrieval$ok) {   n_samples <- 2000   LUT <- as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL, nLUT = n_samples, setseed = 1))   wl <- 400:2500    # Real sun zenith for this acquisition (falls back to the package default   # if the STAC item didn't carry a usable zenith field).   real_tts <- suppressWarnings(mean(as.numeric(retrieval$df_meta$zenith), na.rm = TRUE))   if (is.finite(real_tts)) LUT$tts <- real_tts    # Variable soil brightness (BSM-style range, not one flat value) --   # see Tutorial 03 Section 3.3 for the physical parameters.   set.seed(2)   soil_brightness <- runif(n_samples, 0.05, 0.30)    sim_refl <- t(sapply(seq_len(n_samples), function(i) {     rsoil_i <- rep(soil_brightness[i], length(wl))     foursail(inputLUT = LUT[i, ], rsoil = rsoil_i, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO")$rsot   }))   refl_X <- as.data.frame(sim_refl); colnames(refl_X) <- paste0("X", wl)   refl_X <- cbind(id = seq_len(n_samples), refl_X)   se2a_full <- suppressMessages(get.spectra.convolved(rfl = refl_X, sensor = "Sentinel2a", plot.spectra = FALSE))   names(se2a_full) <- c("id","B1","B2","B3","B4","B5","B6","B7","B8","B8A","B9","B10","B11","B12")    keep <- c("B2","B3","B4","B5","B6","B7","B8","B8A","B11","B12")       # matches the cube's 10 bands   real_names <- c("B02","B03","B04","B05","B06","B07","B08","B8A","B11","B12")   se2a <- se2a_full[, keep]; names(se2a) <- real_names    train_df <- cbind(LUT, se2a)   cat("Real acquisition sun zenith used for training LUT:", round(real_tts, 1), "deg\n") }

what: 4. Does LUT size actually matter here? A convergence check, not an assertion
title: 15. From Satellite Reflectance to Vegetation Traits: Real EO Application
text: Rather assert 2000 enough, test : train several LUT sizes, evaluate every one independent synthetic test set (real image – conflate two different questions), look curve actually flattens:   Accuracy improves LUT size diminishing returns – gain shows well 2000 rows. exactly nuance worth explicit : improvement comes denser coverage , already-reasonable parameter space (real geometry, variable soil, inputsPROSAIL’s trait ranges) size grows, size alone – 2000 rows drawn badly-chosen parameter space show curve.
code: if (retrieval$ok) {   test_lut <- as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL, nLUT = 300, setseed = 999))   test_lut$tts <- LUT$tts[1]   set.seed(3)   test_soil <- runif(300, 0.05, 0.30)   test_refl <- t(sapply(seq_len(300), function(i) {     foursail(inputLUT = test_lut[i, ], rsoil = rep(test_soil[i], length(wl)), LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO")$rsot   }))   test_refl_X <- as.data.frame(test_refl); colnames(test_refl_X) <- paste0("X", wl)   test_refl_X <- cbind(id = seq_len(300), test_refl_X)   test_se2a_full <- suppressMessages(get.spectra.convolved(rfl = test_refl_X, sensor = "Sentinel2a", plot.spectra = FALSE))   names(test_se2a_full) <- names(se2a_full)   test_se2a <- test_se2a_full[, keep]; names(test_se2a) <- real_names    sizes <- c(150, 500, 1000, 2000)   size_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sizes, function(n) {     sub_df <- cbind(LUT[seq_len(n), ], se2a[seq_len(n), ])     fit_n <- get.inversion(data = sub_df, depVar = "LAI", inputs = real_names,                             algorithm = "RF", n.samples = nrow(sub_df), seed = 42)     pred_n <- as.numeric(predict(fit_n$model, newdata = cbind(test_lut, test_se2a)[, c("LAI", real_names)]))     obs_n <- test_lut$LAI     data.frame(n = n, R2 = 1 - sum((obs_n - pred_n)^2) / sum((obs_n - mean(obs_n))^2),                RMSE = sqrt(mean((obs_n - pred_n)^2)))   })) } if (retrieval$ok) {   knitr::kable(size_results, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)   plot(size_results$n, size_results$RMSE, type = "o", pch = 19, col = "#D55E00",        xlab = "LUT size (training rows)", ylab = "RMSE (LAI)", main = "LUT-size convergence, independent test set") }

what: 5. Domain-applicability check: does the real scene actually look like the LUT?
title: 15. From Satellite Reflectance to Vegetation Traits: Real EO Application
text: trained model return prediction input, including reflectance combinations nothing training LUT resembles – real, silent failure mode worth surfacing rather hoping doesn’t happen. Compare real scene’s per-band reflectance range simulated LUT’s:
code: if (retrieval$ok) {   pix_df <- as.data.frame(refl_cube, xy = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE)   ok_rows <- complete.cases(pix_df[, real_names])    domain_tbl <- do.call(rbind, lapply(real_names, function(b) {     lut_range <- range(se2a[[b]])     real_vals <- pix_df[[b]][ok_rows]     data.frame(band = b, lut_min = lut_range[1], lut_max = lut_range[2],                pct_real_outside = round(100 * mean(real_vals < lut_range[1] | real_vals > lut_range[2]), 1))   }))   knitr::kable(domain_tbl, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)    # Flag any pixel with at least one band outside the LUT's simulated range --   # these predictions are extrapolations, not interpolations.   out_of_domain <- rep(FALSE, nrow(pix_df))   for (b in real_names) {     rng <- range(se2a[[b]])     out_of_domain <- out_of_domain | (pix_df[[b]] < rng[1] | pix_df[[b]] > rng[2])   }   out_of_domain[!ok_rows] <- NA   cat("Vegetation pixels with at least one band outside the LUT's simulated range:",       round(100 * mean(out_of_domain[ok_rows & values(veg_mask)[ok_rows] %in% TRUE], na.rm = TRUE), 1), "%\n") } #> Vegetation pixels with at least one band outside the LUT's simulated range: 100 %

title: 15. From Satellite Reflectance to Vegetation Traits: Real EO Application
text: Fit full 2000-row LUT Section 3, predict every pixel, discard predictions outside vegetation mask (Section 2) – whole reason building mask step:  hybrid RTM-derived LAI estimate, validated product. accuracy checked field measurements established satellite LAI product (e.g. Copernicus Global Land, MODIS LAI) – actual next step treating numbers ground truth, something page’s simulated-LUT training can substitute .
code: if (retrieval$ok) {   fit <- get.inversion(data = train_df, depVar = "LAI", inputs = real_names,                         algorithm = "RF", n.samples = nrow(train_df), seed = 42)    pred_lai <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(pix_df))   pred_lai[ok_rows] <- as.numeric(predict(fit$model, newdata = pix_df[ok_rows, real_names]))    veg_vals <- values(veg_mask)[, 1]   pred_lai[!(veg_vals %in% TRUE)] <- NA  # mask out non-vegetation, including NA-NDVI pixels    lai_rast <- refl_cube[["B04"]]  # reuse its grid/extent/crs   values(lai_rast) <- pred_lai   names(lai_rast) <- "LAI_pred"    plot(lai_rast, main = "Vegetation-masked, hybrid-inverted LAI (real Sentinel-2 pixels)")   cat("Predicted LAI range, vegetation pixels only:",       paste(round(range(pred_lai, na.rm = TRUE), 2), collapse = " to "), "\n") } #> [1] "processing hybrid approach using Random Forest ..." #> -0.03662417 0.01  #> 0.06540701 0.01  #> -0.0129615 0.01 #> Predicted LAI range, vegetation pixels only: 2.49 to 3.66

what: 1. L and eps are two different knobs – vary them one at a time first
title: 16. MARMIT + fourSAIL + SPART: Realistic Soil Moisture, Canopy to Atmosphere
text: MARMIT’s wetness controlled two physically distinct parameters: L (water film thickness, cm) eps (fraction surface ’s wet). Varying (“wetness sweep” – Section 3 , deliberately, realistic combined scenario) makes impossible tell one actually driving given change. Vary alone first:   L alone eps alone can drive SMC across nearly whole range (roughly 4% 47%) – neither parameter redundant ; thicker water film larger wet fraction genuinely different physical situations MARMIT’s model treats separately, even though ultimately darken soil.
code: L_seq <- c(0.001, 0.04, 0.08, 0.12, 0.15) soils_L <- lapply(L_seq, function(l) get.marmit.rsoil(database = "Bablet_2016", id = 1, L = l, eps = 0.5, wl.out = 400:2500)) cat("L alone (eps fixed at 0.5) -- SMC (%):", round(sapply(soils_L, function(s) s$SMC), 1), "\n") #> L alone (eps fixed at 0.5) -- SMC (%): 4.1 36 46.7 47.1 47.1  cols_L <- colorRampPalette(c("gold", "saddlebrown"))(length(L_seq)) matplot(soils_L[[1]]$wavelength, sapply(soils_L, function(s) s$rsoil.wet), type = "l", lty = 1, col = cols_L,         xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "Soil reflectance", main = "Varying L alone (eps = 0.5 fixed)") legend("topright", paste("L =", L_seq), col = cols_L, lty = 1, cex = 0.7) eps_seq <- c(0.05, 0.3, 0.55, 0.8, 1.0) soils_eps <- lapply(eps_seq, function(e) get.marmit.rsoil(database = "Bablet_2016", id = 1, L = 0.05, eps = e, wl.out = 400:2500)) cat("eps alone (L fixed at 0.05) -- SMC (%):", round(sapply(soils_eps, function(s) s$SMC), 1), "\n") #> eps alone (L fixed at 0.05) -- SMC (%): 5.6 26.7 43.6 46.7 47  cols_eps <- colorRampPalette(c("gold", "saddlebrown"))(length(eps_seq)) matplot(soils_eps[[1]]$wavelength, sapply(soils_eps, function(s) s$rsoil.wet), type = "l", lty = 1, col = cols_eps,         xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "Soil reflectance", main = "Varying eps alone (L = 0.05 fixed)") legend("topright", paste("eps =", eps_seq), col = cols_eps, lty = 1, cex = 0.7)

what: Why do “Wet” and “Saturated” report almost the same SMC below, despite different spectra?
title: 16. MARMIT + fourSAIL + SPART: Realistic Soil Moisture, Canopy to Atmosphere
text: Worth explaining combined sweep Section 2, since looks like discrepancy otherwise: internally, get.marmit.rsoil() computes phi <- L * eps, estimates SMC phi sigmoid function (SMC = K / (1 + * exp(-psi * phi))) saturates toward ceiling K phi grows. soil’s calibrated sigmoid parameters, ceiling essentially reached phi around 0.07-0.08 – “Wet” (L=0.09, eps=0.8, phi=0.072) “Saturated” (L=0.15, eps=1.0, phi=0.15) land nearly SMC (~47.1%) even though phi still differs factor two. reflectance spectra identical (rsoil.wet differs 0.13 reflectance two) – L eps still influence optical model directly, independent single scalar SMC summary reports. Treat SMC useful one-number summary overall wetness, complete description soil’s optical state.

what: 2. A combined wetness sweep, as a realistic scenario
title: 16. MARMIT + fourSAIL + SPART: Realistic Soil Moisture, Canopy to Atmosphere

code: wetness_steps <- data.frame(   label = c("Very dry", "Dry", "Moderate", "Wet", "Saturated"),   L     = c(0.001, 0.02, 0.05, 0.09, 0.15),   eps   = c(0.05,  0.3,  0.55, 0.8,  1.0) )  soils <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(wetness_steps)), function(i) {   get.marmit.rsoil(database = "Bablet_2016", id = 1, L = wetness_steps$L[i],                     eps = wetness_steps$eps[i], wl.out = 400:2500) })  cat("Estimated soil moisture (SMC, %) across the sweep:\n") #> Estimated soil moisture (SMC, %) across the sweep: print(round(sapply(soils, function(s) s$SMC), 1)) #> [1]  3.8  9.6 43.6 47.1 47.1 wl <- soils[[1]]$wavelength cols <- colorRampPalette(c("gold", "saddlebrown"))(nrow(wetness_steps)) matplot(wl, sapply(soils, function(s) s$rsoil.wet), type = "l", lty = 1, col = cols,         xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "Soil reflectance",         main = "MARMIT soil reflectance across the wetness sweep") legend("topright", wetness_steps$label, col = cols, lty = 1, cex = 0.8)

code: row <- data.frame(   LAI = 2, hspot = 0.01, LIDFa = -0.35, LIDFb = -0.15, TypeLidf = 1,   tts = 30, tto = 0, psi = 0,   N = 1.5, Cab = 40, Car = 8, Anth = 2, Cbrown = 0, EWT = 0.009, LMA = 0.009, alpha = 40 )  toc_by_soil <- sapply(soils, function(s) {   sail_i <- foursail(inputLUT = row, rsoil = s$rsoil.wet, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")   Compute_BRF(rdot = sail_i$rdot, rsot = sail_i$rsot, tts = row$tts, data.light = dataSpec_PDB) })  matplot(dataSpec_PDB[, 1], toc_by_soil, type = "l", lty = 1, col = cols,         xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "TOC reflectance",         main = "Top-of-canopy reflectance, same canopy, soil wetness varied (LAI=2)") legend("topright", wetness_steps$label, col = cols, lty = 1, cex = 0.8)

what: 4. The central result: how the dry-minus-wet signal fades as LAI increases
title: 16. MARMIT + fourSAIL + SPART: Realistic Soil Moisture, Canopy to Atmosphere
text: single figure shows whole page’s physics : full-spectrum difference driest wettest soil Section 2, seven LAI values bare-ish soil closed canopy – just two extremes:  soil-moisture contrast largest across whole spectrum near-bare soil (LAI=0.01) attenuates progressively LAI rises – single-wavelength effect, two-point comparison: SWIR region (1500-1800nm, 2000-2400nm) carries strongest contrast every LAI, consistent MARMIT’s water-absorption physics, attenuation canopy closure visible across full spectrum. canopy configuration, contribution soil-moisture-induced reflectance differences becomes small LAI=6 – “blocked regardless wetness” general rule, specific, quantified attenuation LIDF/hotspot/geometry setup.
code: dry_soil <- soils[[1]]  # "Very dry" wet_soil <- soils[[5]]  # "Saturated"  lai_seq <- c(0.01, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6)  # 0.01 stands in for LAI=0 (foursail needs >0) delta_by_lai <- sapply(lai_seq, function(lai) {   row_i <- row; row_i$LAI <- lai   d <- foursail(inputLUT = row_i, rsoil = dry_soil$rsoil.wet, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")   w <- foursail(inputLUT = row_i, rsoil = wet_soil$rsoil.wet, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")   brf_d <- Compute_BRF(rdot = d$rdot, rsot = d$rsot, tts = row_i$tts, data.light = dataSpec_PDB)   brf_w <- Compute_BRF(rdot = w$rdot, rsot = w$rsot, tts = row_i$tts, data.light = dataSpec_PDB)   brf_d - brf_w  # Delta R(lambda) = R_dry(lambda) - R_wet(lambda) }) cols_lai <- colorRampPalette(c("#B2182B", "#2166AC"))(length(lai_seq)) matplot(dataSpec_PDB[, 1], delta_by_lai, type = "l", lty = 1, col = cols_lai,         xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = expression(Delta*R(lambda) == R[dry](lambda) - R[wet](lambda)),         main = "Soil-moisture contrast vs. wavelength, one curve per LAI") legend("topright", paste("LAI =", lai_seq), col = cols_lai, lty = 1, cex = 0.7, ncol = 2) abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "grey60") cat("Delta R at 1650nm (SWIR, MARMIT's strongest water-sensitive region) across LAI:\n") #> Delta R at 1650nm (SWIR, MARMIT's strongest water-sensitive region) across LAI: print(round(setNames(delta_by_lai[dataSpec_PDB[, 1] == 1650, ], paste0("LAI=", lai_seq)), 4)) #> LAI=0.01  LAI=0.5    LAI=1    LAI=2    LAI=3    LAI=4    LAI=6  #>   0.4873   0.3777   0.2815   0.1456   0.0705   0.0327   0.0064

what: 5. MARMIT + SPART: does the soil-moisture signal survive to the satellite?
title: 16. MARMIT + fourSAIL + SPART: Realistic Soil Moisture, Canopy to Atmosphere
text: Section 4 stopped TOC (canopy-level, atmosphere). SPART() (Tutorial 03) carries MARMIT soil spectrum full soil-plant-atmosphere chain TOA. Band--band, averaged – different Sentinel-2 bands sit different atmospheric transmission windows, mean hide exactly effect worth seeing:  precise “survives” means – depends wavelength. Sentinel-2 bands (B02-B8A, B11, B12) transmit roughly 60-90% TOC soil-moisture contrast TOA – atmosphere attenuates reshapes signal doesn’t erase . two bands sitting inside strong water-vapour absorption windows opposite story: 942nm, ~29% TOC signal survives; 1372nm, essentially none (transmission ~0.008) – atmosphere nearly opaque regardless soil . “atmosphere erase soil signal” true spectrum fixed atmosphere, false specific bands atmospheric absorption dominates – spectrally dependent statement, blanket one, specific one (realistic, sea-level, clear-sky) atmospheric state.
code: soils_spart <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(wetness_steps)), function(i) {   get.marmit.rsoil(database = "Bablet_2016", id = 1, L = wetness_steps$L[i],                     eps = wetness_steps$eps[i], wl.out = 400:2400) })  LUT <- as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = ToolsRTM::inputsSPART, nLUT = 1, setseed = 1)) LUT$Cs <- 0; LUT$fqe <- 0.01; LUT$Cx <- 0 LUT$cell.d <- 40; LUT$inter.c <- 0.045; LUT$baseline.abs <- 0.0006 LUT$leaf.thick <- 1.6; LUT$albino.abs <- 0; LUT$lign.cell <- 2; LUT$Nitrogen <- 1 LUT$Pa <- 1000; LUT$aot550 <- 0.3246; what: 2. Train fourSAIL AND INFORM models on a larger, forest-realistic LUT
title: 17. Monitoring a Forest Site Through Time
text: Two real improvements earlier version page: n_samples 1500 (200), soil sampled across realistic brightness range rather one fixed rsoil = 0.15 – matching Tutorial 15’s LUT-realism argument. LAI constrained 2-7 (plausible closed forest canopy, package’s generic default range). second model, trained inform() simulations instead foursail() (forest crown geometry – sd/cd/h/LAIu – varying , per Tutorial 14’s equifinality finding), lets Section 5 check whether seasonal trajectory actually depends canopy model produced :
code: n_samples <- 1500 LUT <- as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL, nLUT = n_samples, setseed = 1)) LUT$LAI <- runif(n_samples, 2, 7) wl <- 400:2500 set.seed(11) soil_b <- runif(n_samples, 0.05, 0.30) sim_refl <- t(sapply(seq_len(n_samples), function(i) {   foursail(inputLUT = LUT[i, ], rsoil = rep(soil_b[i], length(wl)), LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO")$rsot })) refl_X <- as.data.frame(sim_refl); colnames(refl_X) <- paste0("X", wl) refl_X <- cbind(id = seq_len(n_samples), refl_X) se2a_full <- suppressMessages(get.spectra.convolved(rfl = refl_X, sensor = "Sentinel2a", plot.spectra = FALSE)) names(se2a_full) <- c("id","B1","B2","B3","B4","B5","B6","B7","B8","B8A","B9","B10","B11","B12") keep <- c("B2","B3","B4","B5","B6","B7","B8","B8A","B11","B12") se2a <- se2a_full[, keep]; names(se2a) <- real_names train_df <- cbind(LUT, se2a) fits_sail <- lapply(c("Cab", "LAI", "EWT"), function(trait) {   get.inversion(data = train_df, depVar = trait, inputs = real_names,                 algorithm = "RF", n.samples = nrow(train_df), seed = 42) }) names(fits_sail) <- c("Cab", "LAI", "EWT")  n_inform <- 800 LUT_i <- as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL, nLUT = n_inform, setseed = 2)) # inputsPROSAIL's own LMA row is held fixed at 0 by design (getLUT() samples # Prot/CBC instead, PROSPECT-PRO's dry-matter inputs) -- LeafModel="PROSPECT-D" # below needs LMA directly, so sample it from a typical real-leaf range. LUT_i$LMA <- runif(n_inform, 0.005, 0.02) LUT_i$Cs <- 0; LUT_i$fqe <- 0.01; LUT_i$Cx <- 0 LUT_i$cell.d <- 40; LUT_i$inter.c <- 0.045; LUT_i$baseline.abs <- 0.0006 LUT_i$leaf.thick <- 1.6; LUT_i$albino.abs <- 0; LUT_i$lign.cell <- 2; LUT_i$Nitrogen <- 1 LUT_i$fraction_brown <- 0.1; LUT_i$diss <- 0.5; LUT_i$Cv <- 1; LUT_i$Zeta <- 0 LUT_i$LAI <- runif(n_inform, 2, 7) set.seed(12) LUT_i$LAIu <- runif(n_inform, 0, 0.8); LUT_i$sd <- runif(n_inform, 400, 900) LUT_i$cd <- runif(n_inform, 3, 6); LUT_i$h <- runif(n_inform, 15, 30); LUT_i$skyl <- 0.1 soil_bi <- runif(n_inform, 0.05, 0.30) sim_refl_i <- t(sapply(seq_len(n_inform), function(i) {   suppressMessages(inform(inputLUT = LUT_i[i, ], rsoil = rep(soil_bi[i], length(wl)), LeafModel = "PROSPECT-D")) })) refl_X_i <- as.data.frame(sim_refl_i); colnames(refl_X_i) <- paste0("X", wl) refl_X_i <- cbind(id = seq_len(n_inform), refl_X_i) se2a_full_i <- suppressMessages(get.spectra.convolved(rfl = refl_X_i, sensor = "Sentinel2a", plot.spectra = FALSE)) names(se2a_full_i) <- names(se2a_full) se2a_i <- se2a_full_i[, keep]; names(se2a_i) <- real_names train_df_i <- cbind(LUT_i, se2a_i) fits_inform <- lapply(c("Cab", "LAI", "EWT"), function(trait) {   get.inversion(data = train_df_i, depVar = trait, inputs = real_names,                 algorithm = "RF", n.samples = nrow(train_df_i), seed = 42) }) names(fits_inform) <- c("Cab", "LAI", "EWT")

function(w) {   tryCatch({     sc <- get.satellite_collection(scenario = scenario, collection = "sentinel-2-l2a",                                     cloud_server = "microsoft", n.limit = 20, shape, date_range = w,                                 aggregation_method = "mean", get.dataset = FALSE)     refl <- cube[[real_names]] / 10000      ndvi <- (refl[["B08"]] - refl[["B04"]]) / (refl[["B08"]] + refl[["B04"]])     forest_mask <- ndvi > 0.5  # dense-canopy mask -- excludes roads/clearings/water in the buffer      pix_df <- as.data.frame(refl, na.rm = FALSE)     mvals <- values(forest_mask)[, 1]     ok_rows <- stats::complete.cases(pix_df) & (mvals %in% TRUE)     if (sum(ok_rows) < 5) stop("fewer than 5 forest pixels this window")     pix_ok <- pix_df[ok_rows, ]      ndvi_px <- (pix_ok[["B08"]] - pix_ok[["B04"]]) / (pix_ok[["B08"]] + pix_ok[["B04"]])     ndre_px <- (pix_ok[["B08"]] - pix_ok[["B05"]]) / (pix_ok[["B08"]] + pix_ok[["B05"]])     ndmi_px <- (pix_ok[["B08"]] - pix_ok[["B11"]]) / (pix_ok[["B08"]] + pix_ok[["B11"]])      Cab_sail <- as.numeric(predict(fits_sail$Cab$model, newdata = pix_ok[, real_names]))     LAI_sail <- as.numeric(predict(fits_sail$LAI$model, newdata = pix_ok[, real_names]))     EWT_sail <- as.numeric(predict(fits_sail$EWT$model, newdata = pix_ok[, real_names]))     Cab_inform <- as.numeric(predict(fits_inform$Cab$model, newdata = pix_ok[, real_names]))     LAI_inform <- as.numeric(predict(fits_inform$LAI$model, newdata = pix_ok[, real_names]))      # Domain check (Tutorial 15 Section 5): fraction of forest pixels with at     # least one band outside the fourSAIL LUT's own simulated reflectance range.     out_of_domain <- rep(FALSE, nrow(pix_ok))     for (b in real_names) {       rng <- range(se2a[[b]])       out_of_domain <- out_of_domain | (pix_ok[[b]] < rng[1] | pix_ok[[b]] > rng[2])     }      data.frame(date = as.Date(w[1]), n_forest_px = sum(ok_rows),                NDVI = median(ndvi_px), NDVI_iqr = IQR(ndvi_px),                NDRE = median(ndre_px), NDMI = median(ndmi_px),                Cab_fourSAIL = median(Cab_sail), Cab_fourSAIL_iqr = IQR(Cab_sail),                LAI_fourSAIL = median(LAI_sail), LAI_fourSAIL_iqr = IQR(LAI_sail),                EWT_fourSAIL = median(EWT_sail), EWT_fourSAIL_iqr = IQR(EWT_sail),                Cab_INFORM = median(Cab_inform), LAI_INFORM = median(LAI_inform),                pct_out_of_domain = round(100 * mean(out_of_domain), 1),                ok = TRUE, msg = "")   }, error = function(e) data.frame(date = as.Date(w[1]), n_forest_px = NA_real_,                                      NDVI = NA_real_, NDVI_iqr = NA_real_, NDRE = NA_real_, NDMI = NA_real_, NA_real_, EWT_fourSAIL_iqr = NA_real_,                                      Cab_INFORM = NA_real_, LAI_INFORM = NA_real_,                                      pct_out_of_domain = NA_real_, ok = FALSE, msg = conditionMessage(e))) }  ts_list <- lapply(windows, get_one_date) ts_df <- do.call(rbind, ts_list) print(ts_df[, c("date", "n_forest_px", "NDVI", "Cab_fourSAIL", "Cab_INFORM", Three settings chosen cover real scene LUT later applied (Section 3): LAI 0.3 (inputsPROSAIL’s default lower bound 2 assumes canopy always dense enough optically closed – narrow real forest, includes gaps, edges understory 500m-radius footprint), realistic non-zero sun zenith (25-45°, matching July midday acquisition 52°N, rather package default tts = 0, .e. sun directly overhead), variable soil brightness (0.05-0.30, Tutorial 03’s BSM range, rather one flat rsoil = 0.15). Together widen simulated reflectance envelope enough actually contain real Sentinel-2 pixel values retrieved Section 3 – hybrid-inversion model can trusted inputs fall inside range trained :
code: n_samples <- 500 LUT <- as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL, nLUT = n_samples, setseed = 1)) wl <- 400:2500 set.seed(3) LUT$LAI <- runif(n_samples, 0.3, 5) LUT$tts <- runif(n_samples, 25, 45) soil_brightness <- runif(n_samples, 0.05, 0.30) refl <- t(sapply(seq_len(n_samples), function(i) {   rsoil_i <- rep(soil_brightness[i], length(wl))   foursail(inputLUT = LUT[i, ], rsoil = rsoil_i, LeafModel = "PROSPECT-PRO")$rsot })) refl_X <- as.data.frame(refl); colnames(refl_X) <- paste0("X", wl); refl_X <- cbind(id = seq_len(n_samples), refl_X) se2a_full <- suppressMessages(get.spectra.convolved(rfl = refl_X, sensor = "Sentinel2a", plot.spectra = FALSE)) names(se2a_full) <- c("id","B1","B2","B3","B4","B5","B6","B7","B8","B8A","B9","B10","B11","B12")  keep <- c("B2","B3","B4","B5","B6","B7","B8","B8A","B11","B12") real_names <- c("B02","B03","B04","B05","B06","B07","B08","B8A","B11","B12") se2a <- se2a_full[, keep]; names(se2a) <- real_names  set.seed(1) train_idx <- sample(seq_len(n_samples), size = round(0.7 * n_samples)) train_df <- cbind(LUT[train_idx, ], se2a[train_idx, ]) fit_cab <- get.inversion(data = train_df, depVar = "Cab", inputs = real_names,                           algorithm = "RF", n.samples = nrow(train_df), seed = 42)

what: 2. Vegetation mask and spectral indices at native resolution
title: 19. FLEX Cal/Val: ESU Heterogeneity Mapping and Trait Retrieval at FLEX Scale
text: get.sentinel2_cube() already applies Sentinel-2’s SCL cloud/shadow/snow mask internally (Tutorial 15). NDVI separates vegetated non-vegetated pixels within buffer – roads, clearings, water. Computed two ways , deliberately: direct formula, independently via real package function getSpatial_index() (expects standard 12-band Sentinel-2 layout, two missing 60m-bands pipeline doesn’t retrieve – B01, B09 – padded NA first; aren’t used NDVI calculation ):
code: ndvi10 <- (refl10[["B08"]] - refl10[["B04"]]) / (refl10[["B08"]] + refl10[["B04"]]) names(ndvi10) <- "NDVI" veg_mask <- ndvi10 > 0.5  # Cross-check against getSpatial_index(), the real package function b01_na <- b09_na <- refl10[["B02"]]; terra::values(b01_na) <- NA; terra::values(b09_na) <- NA r12 <- c(b01_na, refl10[["B02"]], refl10[["B03"]], refl10[["B04"]], refl10[["B05"]],          refl10[["B06"]], refl10[["B07"]], refl10[["B08"]], refl10[["B8A"]], b09_na,          refl10[["B11"]], refl10[["B12"]]) names(r12) <- c("B01","B02","B03","B04","B05","B06","B07","B08","B8A","B09","B11","B12") tmp12 <- tempfile(fileext = ".tif") terra::writeRaster(r12 * 10000, tmp12, overwrite = TRUE)  # getSpatial_index expects raw DN, applies its own factorR ndvi_pkg <- getSpatial_index(rasterFiles = tmp12, Sensor = "Sentinel2a", SpectraltoCompute = "NDVI", factorR = 1/10000)[[1]] max_diff <- max(abs(terra::values(ndvi10) - terra::values(ndvi_pkg)), na.rm = TRUE) cat("Max abs diff, hand-computed NDVI vs. getSpatial_index():", max_diff, "\n") #> Max abs diff, hand-computed NDVI vs. getSpatial_index(): 3.695741e-08  ndre10 <- (refl10[["B8A"]] - refl10[["B05"]]) / (refl10[["B8A"]] + refl10[["B05"]]) names(ndre10) <- "NDRE" ndre_veg <- terra::mask(ndre10, veg_mask, maskvalue = FALSE)  plot(ndre_veg, main = "NDRE (vegetation-masked, 10m, Loobos)", col = colorRampPalette(c("khaki","darkgreen"))(50))

title: The ToolsRTM package
text: tutorial provides overview ToolsRTM packages, developed using R Markdown Notebook. ToolsRTM package essential R package integrates key radiative transfer (RT) models simulating canopy reflectance across hyperspectral, Sentinel-2, various satellite scales. versatile package includes numerous functions estimating plant traits, calculating spectral indices, generating time series data. Additionally, facilitates validation predictions comparisons field observations. Currently testing phase, ToolsRTM package equipped robust suite tools designed simulating canopy reflectance using range RT models diverse satellite resolutions. Key models include INFORM, fourSAIL, fourSAIL2 canopy-scale simulations, well PROSPECT (D PRO variants), Liberty, FLUSPECT (B-Cx) leaf-level simulations. comprehensive package empowers users conduct detailed simulations across various scales models, enabling versatile accurate analyses canopy reflectance characteristics.  Fig. 1 Simulation using several biophysical models. ToolsRTM package integrated ToolsRTM Simulator app, relies two key R packages optimal functionality. packages essential efficiently simulating executing functions within server. ToolsRTM Package: comprehensive package consolidates various RT models simulating reflectance Top Canopy (TOC). incorporates several canopy models, fourSAIL, fourSAIL2, INFORM, along leaf models. Additionally, ToolsRTM package includes Soil-Plant-Atmosphere Radiative Transfer (SPART) model, simulates Top--Atmosphere (TOA) reflectance integrating atmospheric parameters. SPART employs three computationally efficient sub-models—BSM soil, PROSAIL vegetation canopies, SMAC atmospheric effects—ensuring accurate simulation directional TOA observations. SCOPEin Package: SCOPEin R package designed execute Soil Canopy Observation, Photochemistry, Energy fluxes (SCOPE) radiative transfer model. Originally developed MATLAB Van der Tol et al. (2009) extended Yang et al. (2020), SCOPEin R enables seamless integration SCOPE model within R environment, offering users flexibility harness capabilities -depth analysis. ToolsRTM SCOPEinR part RTM-Suite, also ships point--click Shiny app (code required) covering models – see Apps/RTMs, runnable locally via shiny::runApp("Apps/RTMs"). code: inputsPRO <- ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL nSamples =200 LUT<-as.data.frame(getLUT(inputs = inputsPRO, nLUT=nSamples, setseed = 1234))  no_cores <- detectCores() - 2 cl <- makeCluster(no_cores) registerDoParallel(cl)  sim.rfl<-list() sims<-foreach(i=1:nSamples) %dopar% {    data.foursail_pro<-ToolsRTM::foursail(inputLUT=LUT[i,],rsoil=rsoil.default,                                         LeafModel = 'PROSPECT-PRO',spectrum.all = T)   rdot<-data.foursail_pro[[1]]   rsot<-data.foursail_pro[[2]]   data.foursail_pro<-ToolsRTM::Compute_BRF(rdot=rdot,rsot=rsot,tts=LUT[i,'tts'],                                            data.light =ToolsRTM::dataSpec_PDB)    sim.rfl[[i]]<-data.foursail_pro   } ##end paralle  stopCluster(cl)

what: 3.6 Example: Spectral Resampling to Sentinel-2a resolution
title: The ToolsRTM package
text: example, perform spectral resampling simulated canopy reflectance data match spectral resolution Sentinel-2a. signal::interp1() function used linear interpolation resample reflectance original wavelength range (400-2500 nm) center wavelengths Sentinel-2a bands. resampled reflectance visualized ggplot2. Key Steps: Interpolation: reflectance data interpolated original wavelength range (400-2500 nm) match Sentinel-2a spectral bands. Visualization: resampled reflectance values plotted function wavelength simulation, colors indicating different trait values. Summary Statistics: Average, median, percentile values (5th 95th) calculated wavelength band provide summary reflectance distribution across simulations.  plot shows canopy reflectance changes across Sentinel-2a spectral bands, line representing reflectance specific simulation, allowing clear visualization spectral resampling process.
code: sim.canopy<-as.matrix(do.call(rbind,sims))   wave<-c(400:2500)   depVar = 'Cab'    waves.se2 <- subset(ToolsRTM::sensor.characteristics, Sensor == 'Sentinel2a')   center_wvl <- waves.se2$average    # Initialize an empty list to store interpolated reflectance data   SE2_df <- list()   refl.se2 <- list()   # Perform linear interpolation for each row in sim.canopy   for (i in 1:nrow(sim.canopy)) {     # Perform linear interpolation to resample to Sentinel-2 bands     reflectance.i <- signal::interp1(wave, sim.canopy[i, ], center_wvl, method = "spline")     # Store the interpolated reflectance in the list     SE2_df[[i]] <- data.frame(center_wvl = center_wvl, reflectance = reflectance.i,                               n.sim=i,trait=LUT[,depVar][i])     refl.se2[[i]] <- reflectance.i   }    # Convert the list to a matrix   df.SE2 <- do.call(rbind, SE2_df)   df.rfl.SE2 <- do.call(rbind, refl.se2)    # Calculate average, 25th percentile, and 50th percentile for each band   stats.SE2 <- df.SE2 %>%     group_by(center_wvl) %>%     summarise(       average = mean(reflectance,na.rm=T),       median = median(reflectance,na.rm=T),       percentile_05 = quantile(reflectance, 0.05,na.rm=T),       percentile_50 = quantile(reflectance, 0.50,na.rm=T),       percentile_95 = quantile(reflectance, 0.95,na.rm=T)     )   # Define the colors for the greens   gradient_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("cornsilk4",'gold3', "darkolivegreen4"))(nSamples)    # ggplot scatter plot with modifications   plot.ind <- ggplot(df.SE2, aes(x = center_wvl, y = reflectance,color=as.factor(trait))) + #ylim(0,1) +     #geom_tile(aes(color = trait), width = 1) +     geom_line(size = 1,alpha=0.5) +     scale_color_manual(values = gradient_colors) +     theme_bw() +     theme(legend.position="none",           plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=10,face="bold"),           panel.background = element_rect(fill="grey87"),           axis.title = element_text(face="bold", size=14),           axis.text.y=element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=12,face="bold"),           axis.text.x=element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=12,face="bold"),           legend.title=element_blank())   print(plot.ind)

text: example, calculate key spectral indices resampled Sentinel-2a reflectance data. indices derived resampled spectral bands using pre-defined Sentinel-2a spectral indices functions. indices provide insights various plant traits like chlorophyll content canopy structure. Key Steps: Resampled Reflectance: reflectance data, previously resampled Sentinel-2a bands, converted wide format index calculation. Spectral Indices Calculation: Using ToolsRTM::getIndicesSE2() function, set commonly used spectral indices (e.g., CR.red.nir) calculated simulation based Sentinel-2a bands. Visualization: relationship chlorophyll content (Cab) computed spectral index (CR.red.nir) visualized scatter plot using ggplot2. color gradient reflects variations Cab trait values, helping illustrate chlorophyll content influences spectral indices.  plot highlights sensitivity CR-re.nir index changes Cab, showing parameter affects reflectance behavior specific spectral regions.
code: # Convert resampled list to wide format df   SE2_wide <- tidyr::pivot_wider(df.SE2, names_from = c("center_wvl"), values_from = c("reflectance"))   SE2_wide <- tidyr::unnest(SE2_wide,names(SE2_wide))    # Rename bands   names(SE2_wide) <- c('n.sim','trait','B1','B2','B3','B4','B5','B6','B7','B8','B8A','B9','B10','B11','B12')   # Calculate indices   SE2.bands <- c('B1','B2','B3','B4','B5','B6','B7','B8','B8A','B9','B10','B11','B12')   SE2.ind <- ToolsRTM::getIndicesSE2(SE2_wide[,SE2.bands], sensor = "Sentinel-2a", df.data = NULL, fast.process =T)    # Combine LUT, bands and indices   LUT_SE2 <- cbind(LUT,SE2_wide)   LUT_SE2_Indices <- cbind(LUT,SE2_wide,SE2.ind) # Define the colors for the greens   gradient_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("cornsilk4",'gold3', "darkolivegreen4"))(200)    # Create a ggplot scatter plot with modifications   plot.ind <- ggplot(LUT_SE2_Indices, aes_string(x = depVar, y = 'CR.red.nir',color=depVar)) +     geom_point(size = 5,alpha=0.8) +     viridis::scale_color_viridis() +     # Add plot title and legend title   labs(title = "Changes in chorophyll content", color = 'Cab') +      theme_bw() +     theme(legend.position="right",           plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=14,face="bold"),           panel.background = element_rect(fill="grey87"),           axis.title = element_text(face="bold", size=14),           axis.text.y=element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=12,face="bold"),           axis.text.x=element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=12,face="bold"),           legend.title=element_blank())   print(plot.ind)

title: A Package for Simulating RT Models
text: ToolsRTM package provides comprehensive suite tools simulating canopy reflectance using various radiative transfer (RT) models multiple satellite resolutions. Currently testing phase, package designed facilitate detailed simulations, enabling versatile accurate analyses canopy reflectance characteristics. ToolsRTM documentation — Package Simulating RT Models canopy-level simulations, package features models INFORM, fourSAIL, fourSAIL2. comes leaf-level simulations, includes PROSPECT model (D PRO variants), Liberty, FLUSPECT (B-Cx). models empower users conduct sophisticated simulations capture intricate dynamics reflectance behavior leaf canopy contexts.  Fig. 1. Simulations performed ToolsRTM Package several radiative transfer models . Additionally, SPART model (Soil-Plant-Atmosphere Radiative Transfer model) tailored satellite measurements solar spectrum. integrates three computationally efficient RT models: BSM model soil, PROSAIL vegetation canopies, SMAC atmosphere. components interconnected using four-stream theory adding method, allowing SPART simulate directional top--atmosphere (TOA) spectral observations. approach accounts significant effects, sun-observer geometries non-Lambertian reflectance land surface. ToolsRTM includes MARMIT (Multilayer rAdiative tRansfer Model soIl reflecTance), radiative transfer model simulating spectral reflectance bare soil function surface water content. MARMIT simulates soil reflectance across 400–2500 nm spectral range 1 nm resolution. high-level get.marmit.rsoil() wrapper, built get.marmit1() get.marmit2(), loads dry-soil reference spectrum runs MARMIT simulation directly. package includes Bablet 2016 soil database default keep installation lightweight. Seven additional MARMIT soil databases available RTM-Suite databases/ directory: Dupiau 2020 Humper 2015 Lesaignoux 2008 Liu 2002 Lobell 2002 Marcq 2012 Philpot 2014 Together, databases represent approximately 200 MB additional soil spectral data. can used directly get.marmit.rsoil() specifying location db_root argument, without copying files R package.

title: A Package for Simulating RT Models
text: ToolsRTM port several radiative transfer models bundled behind one common R interface, carry license. Three bundled models – Fluspect-B, fourSAIL2, SPART – ports GPL-3.0-licensed original models, GPL-3.0 requires combined work incorporating GPL-3.0 code distributed GPL-3.0 whole. ToolsRTM therefore distributed GPL-3.0 (License: GPL-3 DESCRIPTION), matching Python port toolsrtm’s license. Within GPL-3.0 distribution, two kinds code coexist: ported radiative transfer models (leaf canopy functions listed THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md) – GPL-3.0 three GPL-derived ports , independently MIT-licensable rest (e.g. PROSPECT-D/-PRO). Original utilities developed package– LUT generation (getLUT, getLUTs, getLUT_liberty), spectral indices (getIndices, getIndices_SE2*, getSpectraIndices), sensor convolution wrappers (Spectral.convolution, get.spectral.convolution.*, get.smac, get.coef.SMAC), sensitivity analysis (get.sobol.indices), trait-inversion tooling (get.inversion, get.inversionOpt, hybrid_inversion, hybrid_inversionE, carspls, get.cars.pls, getVIF) – original, independent work MIT individually. title: Get Convolved Spectra — get.spectra.convolved
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ #spectral response function downloaded from: #https://oceancolor.gsfc.nasa.gov/resources/docs/rsr_tables/  # 1. Generate a Lookup Table (LUT) for PROSAIL inputs  inputs.prosail <- ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL # Create a LUT with 1 entry using the defined PROSAIL inputs df.LUT <- as.data.frame(ToolsRTM::getLUT(inputs = inputs.prosail, nLUT = 1, setseed = 1234))  # 2. Simulate spectral reflectance using PROSAIL and apply BRDF effect  # Simulate reflectance values using the PROSAIL model for the first LUT entry reflectance_values <- ToolsRTM::foursail(inputLUT = df.LUT[1,], rsoil = rsoil,                                           LeafModel = 'PROSPECT-PRO') rdot <- reflectance_values[[1]]  # Direct reflectance rsot <- reflectance_values[[2]]  # Diffuse reflectance  # Compute the Bidirectional Reflectance Factor (BRF) using BRDF effects reflectance_values <- ToolsRTM::Compute_BRF(rdot = rdot, rsot = rsot,                                             tts = df.LUT[1, 'tts'],                                             data.light = ToolsRTM::dataSpec_PDB) # Convert the reflectance values to a matrix for further processing sim.matrix <- as.matrix(t(reflectance_values)) colnames(sim.matrix)=paste0("X",wavelength) # 3. Convolve the simulated reflectance with a sensor-specific SRF and plot the result  # Here, we use the Sentinel-2A sensor for spectral resampling and plotting convolved_spectra <- get.spectra.convolved(rfl = sim.matrix, sensor = "Sentinel2a",                                             plot.spectra = TRUE) } # }

text: get.spectral.convolution.rfl() needs SMAC atmospheric-correction coefficients bundled; get.spectral.convolution.srf() needs real, measured, per-nm SRF table. Neither exists sensors – often published (student , e.g. instrument's ENVI header, camera calibration sheet) list band center wavelengths full widths half maximum (FWHM). function covers case, three possible inputs:

title: Convolve reflectance onto a sensor using only NOMINAL band characteristics (center wavelength + FWHM, or center + band edges) – for sensors with no real measured per-nm SRF curve available at all, approximated as a Gaussian response (optionally truncated to a published band edge range). — get.spectral.convolution.gaussian

title: Convolve reflectance onto a sensor using only NOMINAL band characteristics (center wavelength + FWHM, or center + band edges) – for sensors with no real measured per-nm SRF curve available at all, approximated as a Gaussian response (optionally truncated to a published band edge range). — get.spectral.convolution.gaussian
text: df data frame wave column (wavelength, nm) rfl column (reflectance) – convention get.spectral.convolution.rfl()/get.spectral.convolution.srf(). Used SINGLE spectrum; many spectra (e.g. entire LUT), use rfl/wave instead (see ) – much faster, vectorized one matrix multiplication instead one call per row. sensor.Optional: bundled sensor name (see ). given, centers/fwhm looked automatically values also pass ignored. centers Optional (required sensor.given): sensor's band center wavelengths, nm. fwhm Optional: sensor's per-band FWHM, nm, length order centers. Derived band spacing omitted. get.plots logical, plot convolved spectrum? Default FALSE. Ignored rfl/wave (bulk mode) used instead df. rfl Optional: matrix data.frame MANY reflectance spectra , one row per spectrum, columns matching wave (e.g. LUT's simulated reflectance matrix). supplied (together wave), df ignored whole matrix convolved one vectorized pass – fast path large tables. wave Required together rfl: wavelength grid (nm) rfl's columns .

title: Convolve reflectance onto a sensor using only NOMINAL band characteristics (center wavelength + FWHM, or center + band edges) – for sensors with no real measured per-nm SRF curve available at all, approximated as a Gaussian response (optionally truncated to a published band edge range). — get.spectral.convolution.gaussian
text: Single-spectrum mode (df): data frame one row per band: band (index), wl (center wavelength, nm), fwhm (nm), RFL (convolved reflectance) – sorted wl. Bulk mode (rfl/wave): numeric matrix, one row per input spectrum (row order rfl), one column per band (named center wavelength, sorted wl); per-band wl/fwhm vectors attached attr(, "wl") / attr(, "fwhm").

title: Convolve reflectance onto a sensor using only NOMINAL band characteristics (center wavelength + FWHM, or center + band edges) – for sensors with no real measured per-nm SRF curve available at all, approximated as a Gaussian response (optionally truncated to a published band edge range). — get.spectral.convolution.gaussian
text: sensor.= "EnMAP" – ToolsRTM::EnMap.characteristics's 242 channels (center + FWHM already given). sensor.= one unique(ToolsRTM::sensor.characteristics$Sensor) ("ALI", "Hyperion", "Landsat4", "Landsat5", "Landsat7", "Landsat8", "MODIS", "Quickbird", "RapidEye", "Sentinel2a", "Sentinel2b", "WorldView2-4", "WorldView2-8") – ship published band edges (lb/ub), FWHM directly; FWHM derived ub - lb Gaussian response additionally hard-truncated [lb, ub] (convention get.srf.from_fwhm() already uses sensors). (Sentinel-2A/B PRISMA REAL measured SRF table bundled instead – use get.spectral.convolution.srf() , accurate Gaussian approximation.) sensor/camera: supply centers , nm (e.g. copied straight ENVI header's wavelength = {...} block). fwhm optional – omitted, band's width approximated distance neighboring bands (standard assumption CONTIGUOUS pushbroom imaging spectrometer, e.g. Headwall camera, true per-band SRF calibration available). know band's real FWHM (e.g. camera datasheet, ENVI header includes fwhm = {...} block), pass explicitly accurate result.

title: Convolve reflectance onto a sensor using only NOMINAL band characteristics (center wavelength + FWHM, or center + band edges) – for sensors with no real measured per-nm SRF curve available at all, approximated as a Gaussian response (optionally truncated to a published band edge range). — get.spectral.convolution.gaussian
code: df <- data.frame(wave = ToolsRTM::dataSpec_PDB[, 1],                   rfl = 0.05 + 0.3 * ToolsRTM::dataSpec_PDB[, 1] / 2500)  # A bundled sensor with only nominal characteristics (no measured SRF): enmap_bands <- get.spectral.convolution.gaussian(df, sensor.i = "EnMAP") modis_bands <- get.spectral.convolution.gaussian(df, sensor.i = "MODIS")  # Your OWN sensor -- e.g. a 3-camera 15-band synchronized rig, with # known band center + FWHM for every band: own_centers <- c(444, 475, 502, 531, 550, 560, 570, 650, 668, 678, 705, 717, 740, 754, 842) own_fwhm    <- c(28,  32,  18,  14,  12,  27,  14,  16,  14,  14,  10,  12,  18,  10,  57) own_bands <- get.spectral.convolution.gaussian(df, centers = own_centers, fwhm = own_fwhm)  # A pushbroom imaging spectrometer's own band list from its ENVI header # (e.g. a Headwall camera) -- only wavelength centers known, no FWHM: headwall_centers <- c(398.02, 400.25, 402.48, 404.71, 406.94)  # (truncated example) headwall_bands <- get.spectral.convolution.gaussian(df, centers = headwall_centers)  # Bulk mode: an entire LUT's reflectance matrix at once (fast, vectorized) wave <- 400:2500 rfl_matrix <- matrix(0.05 + 0.3 * wave / 2500, nrow = 50, ncol = length(wave), byrow = TRUE) bulk_bands <- get.spectral.convolution.gaussian(centers = own_centers, fwhm = own_fwhm,                                                  rfl = rfl_matrix, wave = wave)

what: Spectral global sensitivity analysis (Johnson relative importance per wavelength) — get.spectral.sensitivity
title: Spectral global sensitivity analysis (Johnson relative importance per wavelength) — get.spectral.sensitivity
text: Runs canopy radiative transfer model many times varying set plant/soil traits, computes Johnson relative-importance index (get.sobol.indices's .Johnson_norm column, via sensitivity::johnson()) wavelength – .e. much trait relatively contributes explaining reflectance variance wavelength. Produces data behind stacked "relative contribution (percent) vs wavelength" plot (traits stacked 100 percent every wavelength). Despite name, use get.sobol.indices()'s STi (total Sobol index) column – column known bug (see ToolsRTM/R/get.sobol.indices.R function's source comments) produces near-uniform, physically-meaningless split across traits; .Johnson_norm metric package's reference sensitivity scripts (TOcheck/sensibilidad/) already use exact figure.

title: Spectral global sensitivity analysis (Johnson relative importance per wavelength) — get.spectral.sensitivity
code: get.spectral.sensitivity(   n.samples = 1000,   distribution = "Uniform",   traits = c("N", "Cab", "EWT", "LMA", "LIDFa", "LAI"),   leaf.model = "PROSPECT-D",   canopy.model = "fourSAIL",   rsoil.base = NULL,   wl.step = 5,   seed = 123,   n.cores = NULL,   chunk.size = 500,   save.path = NULL )

title: Spectral global sensitivity analysis (Johnson relative importance per wavelength) — get.spectral.sensitivity
text: n.samples integer. Number RTM simulations run (also total number rows fed get.sobol.indices, whose N parameter set n.samples / 2, internal split-half sample size). Default 1000, matching 500 used actual Sobol calculation. distribution character. "Uniform" "Gaussian" – PDF varied trait drawn (bounds/mean+sd come ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL). traits character vector. trait names (must exist ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL$variable) vary attribute sensitivity . Default: N, Cab, EWT, LMA, LIDFa, LAI – plus SoilCoef (soil-brightness multiplier, 0.5-1.5, flat baseline soil spectrum) added automatically, matching classic PROSAIL sensitivity figure (leaf structure, pigment, water, dry matter, leaf angle, LAI, soil). leaf.model, canopy.model character. Passed simulate_RTM. rsoil.base numeric. Baseline soil reflectance spectrum (SoilCoef multiplier); default flat 0.15 across 400-2500nm. wl.step integer. Compute Sobol indices every wl.step nm instead every single nm, speed (Sobol calculation , RTM simulations, dominates runtime full 1nm resolution). Default 5. seed integer. Random seed reproducibility. n.cores integer. Number cores parallel simulation loop (via parallel/doParallel, pattern Scripts/Sensibility). Default parallel::detectCores() - 2. chunk.size integer. Simulations run chunks size (default 500) instead , matching chunking pattern Scripts/1-getSCOPE-v3_withChunck.R. keeps memory bounded large n.samples (5000, 20000, ...) , save.path given, means crash partway loses -progress chunk, whole run. save.path character NULL. given, chunk's raw simulated reflectance + LUT rows saved file.path(save.path, "chunk_<>.rds") soon chunk finishes (results survive crash/interrupt), read back disk (re-simulated) files already exist – re-running save.path resumes instead restarting.

title: Run a vegetation reflectance/energy-balance simulation, choosing models interactively — run_simulation
text: single entry point tying ToolsRTM SCOPEinR together. Two simulation types supported:

title: Run a vegetation reflectance/energy-balance simulation, choosing models interactively — run_simulation
code: run_simulation(   simulation.type = "optical",   inputLUT,   rsoil = NULL,   leaf.model = "PROSPECT-PRO",   canopy.model = "fourSAIL",   optipar = NULL,   options.SCOPE = NULL,   parallel = FALSE,   get.outputs = "ALL",   get.plots = FALSE,   ... )

title: Run a vegetation reflectance/energy-balance simulation, choosing models interactively — run_simulation
text: simulation.type character. "optical" (ToolsRTM , canopy reflectance) "scope" (SCOPEinR, full energy balance). Default "optical". inputLUT one row ("optical") full multi-row LUT ("scope") biophysical parameters. rsoil soil reflectance spectrum. Required "optical"; ignored "scope" (SCOPEinR builds options.SCOPE). leaf.model character. Leaf model name. "optical": "PROSPECT-PRO", "PROSPECT-D", "Liberty", "Fluspect-B", "Fluspect-B-Cx". "scope": SCOPEinR's naming, e.g. "fluspect-CX". canopy.model character. Canopy model name. "optical": "fourSAIL", "foursail2", "INFORM" (three real canopy models ToolsRTM). "scope": SCOPEinR's naming, e.g. "fourSAIL". optipar optical parameters. "optical", passed Fluspect variants used. "scope", passed SCOPEinR (e.g. SCOPEinR::optipar2021.Pro.CX). options.SCOPE SCOPE run-options table (used simulation.type = "scope" – see SCOPEinR's documentation structure). parallel logical. "scope" : run parallel via SCOPEinR::get.SCOPE.parallel() instead SCOPEinR::get.SCOPE(). Default FALSE. get.outputs character. "scope" : SCOPE outputs return, e.g. "". Default "". get.plots logical. "scope" : whether SCOPEinR generate diagnostic plots. Default FALSE. ... additional arguments passed underlying simulate_RTM() / SCOPEinR call.

title: Run a vegetation reflectance/energy-balance simulation, choosing models interactively — run_simulation
text: "optical": output simulate_RTM() (reflectance components). "scope": output SCOPEinR's get.SCOPE()/get.SCOPE.parallel() (reflectance, fluorescence, radiance, energy-balance fluxes).

title: Run a vegetation reflectance/energy-balance simulation, choosing models interactively — run_simulation
text: "optical" – canopy reflectance , atmosphere/energy balance. Runs entirely within ToolsRTM via simulate_RTM(). Fast, good building large LUTs inversion. "scope" – full Soil-Canopy-Observation-Photochemistry-Energy balance simulation (reflectance + fluorescence + radiance + energy fluxes), via SCOPEinR. Requires SCOPEinR package installed – function checks explicitly gives informative error (real GitLab install command) rather cryptic "find function" missing, since SCOPEinR companion package, hard dependency ToolsRTM. function invent simulation logic : "optical" path calls existing, tested simulate_RTM(); "scope" path calls SCOPEinR's get.SCOPE() / get.SCOPE.parallel() using argument names confirmed real teaching scripts using packages together.

title: Run a vegetation reflectance/energy-balance simulation, choosing models interactively — run_simulation
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Optical-only simulation (ToolsRTM alone, fast, no energy balance) inputs <- ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL LUT <- as.data.frame(ToolsRTM::getLUT(inputs = inputs, nLUT = 1, setseed = 1234)) sim <- run_simulation(   simulation.type = "optical",   inputLUT = LUT[1, ], rsoil = rsoil,   leaf.model = "PROSPECT-PRO", canopy.model = "fourSAIL" )  # Full SCOPE simulation with energy balance (needs SCOPEinR installed) scope_opts <- read.table("Tables/inputs/setoptions.csv", header = TRUE, sep = ",") sim_scope <- run_simulation(   simulation.type = "scope",   inputLUT = LUT, options.SCOPE = scope_opts,   optipar = SCOPEinR::optipar2021.Pro.CX,   leaf.model = "fluspect-CX", canopy.model = "fourSAIL",   parallel = TRUE, get.outputs = "ALL" ) } # }

title: ToolsRTM 0.62.5
text: Replaced single comprehensive ToolsRTM vignette handful standalone articles full numbered tutorial series (18 vignettes, 01-getting-started 18-spatial-index-mapping), covering leaf/ canopy radiative transfer, SPART, model comparison, LUT construction, parallel simulation, hyperspectral/VNIR sensor convolution, vegetation indices, sensitivity analysis, hybrid/ML/deep-learning inversion, full end--end pipeline, closing real-data applications: live Sentinel-2 retrieval via STAC genuine spatial trait/index maps two real Dutch forest sites (Speulderbos, Loobos), real multi-date forest time series. pre-existing comprehensive manuals (ToolsRTM, Getting-LUTs, InversionOpt, course-pipeline, model-comparison--sensitivity) kept alongside new series deeper reference material. Network-dependent (live STAC/Sentinel-2) TensorFlow/PyTorch-dependent tutorials moved vignettes/articles/ (pkgdown-articles, built checked package vignettes) R CMD check/CRAN builds stay fast network-independent.

title: ToolsRTM 0.62.5
text: Real bugs found fixed building/verifying tutorial series (confirmed known physics direct numerical comparison, just code inspection): get.plots argument handling SPART() ignored caller’s actual value forced TRUE whenever argument supplied . Compute_BRF()’s short.waves handling silently recycled solar- irradiance vectors instead truncating Fluspect’s shorter spectral domain argument omitted. foursail2() never truncated rsoil Fluspect leaf models, silently recycling full-length soil spectrum shorter leaf-optics domain throughout SAIL2 core. getFluspect.B()/getFluspect.Cx() returned NULL (rather valid zero-fluorescence output) whenever fqe = 0, crashing every downstream caller zero-length reflectance/transmittance vector. get.spectral.convolution.rfl() mislabelled band-center wavelengths 6 9 bundled sensors (Landsat 4/5/7, Sentinel-3A/B OLCI, Terra/Aqua MODIS) due column-ordering assumption happened hold Sentinel-2. get.sentinel2_cube() get.satellite_collection() called rstac/ gdalcubes/terra functions without namespace-qualifying , fresh session library(ToolsRTM) attached failed “find function” errors; now fully namespace-qualified work standalone. get.inversion(algorithm = "Ensemble") referenced undefined fmla.n variable passed wrong argument shape caret::createFolds() internal caretEnsemble stacking step. get.sobol.indices()’s STi (total Sobol index) column formula bug (never referenced actual input variable), producing near- uniform, physically meaningless split across traits; get.spectral. sensitivity() now uses function’s separately-correct .Johnson_norm column instead. get.sentinel2_cube()’s NDVI-band-arithmetic output checked wrong class name ("RasterLayer" instead "SpatRaster") raster--terra migration downstream Shiny apps, silently disabling NDVI-included GeoTIFF download path.

title: ToolsRTM 0.62.5
text: Migrated every remaining use archived/legacy raster package terra across package source bundled Shiny apps (raster removed Imports); repo-wide grep -rl "raster::" (excluding generated documentation) now returns nothing. Removed two redundant staging copies TOcheck/ already properly ported package source.

title: ToolsRTM 0.1.0 - 0.62.5 (prior to this changelog)
text: Initial development: PROSPECT-D/-PRO, Liberty, Fluspect-B/-Cx leaf models; fourSAIL, fourSAIL2, INFORM canopy models; SPART soil-plant- atmosphere model; MARMIT soil reflectance model; LUT generation correlated sampling; sensor convolution (measured SRF, SMAC-bundled, Gaussian--nominal-characteristics); vegetation indices; hybrid, classical-ML (caret, 12 algorithms), deep-learning (TensorFlow/ Keras) trait inversion; real Sentinel-2 retrieval via STAC.
